title: Joint Time Delay and Frequency Offset Estimation in vMIMO-Beamforming Relays with Population-Based Techniques and Importance Sampling.
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of joint time delay (TD) and carrier frequency offset (CFO) estimation in virtual multiple-input multiple-output (vMIMO) decode-andforward relay systems. A data-aided (DA) maximum likelihood (ML) estimation framework is developed by combining population-based metaheuristic optimization methods with importance sampling (IS). Three optimization algorithms are considered: particle swarm optimization (PSO), grey wolf optimization (GWO), and differential evolution (DE). While these methods provide global search capabilities, their performance may be limited by convergence speed and estimation accuracy in high-dimensional parameter spaces. To address this issue, IS is incorporated into each algorithm to guide the generation of candidate solutions. The resulting hybrid estimators, namely IS-PSO, IS-GWO (or GWOEIS), and IS-DE, leverage pseudoprobability density functions to improve the exploration of the parameter space. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed estimators achieve improved TD and CFO estimation performance compared to their original counterparts and conventional expectation-maximization-based techniques.

title: Low-PAPR Channel Estimation for MIMO-OTFS Systems via Embedded Pilot Codes.
abstract: This paper proposes a delay-Doppler (DD) domain channel estimation scheme for Orthogonal Time-Frequency Space (OTFS) modulation that utilizes embedded pilot codes to overcome the limitations of traditional single-symbol methods. By embedding a sequence with low autocorrelation sidelobes, such as a Barker code, into the transmit grid, the transmitter spreads pilot energy across multiple bins. At the receiver, the DD channel transfer function is estimated through cross-correlation, leveraging the code's ideal autocorrelation properties to achieve high precision. This approach significantly improves the Peak-to-Average-Power Ratio (PAPR) by avoiding the high-power spikes of single-symbol pilots while maintaining robust performance and bit error rate convergence even in low-SNR environments. We further extend this to MIMO-OTFS systems by employing a set of pilot codes with low mutual crosscorrelation, allowing for simultaneous multi-antenna channel estimation with minimal guard band overhead and maintained power efficiency.

title: Decentralized Learning Framework for Anomaly Detection in Integrated UAV and CAV Ecosystems.
abstract: The simultaneous operation of multiple autonomous vehicles, including Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), is transforming intelligent transportation systems by enhancing communication, collaborative assessment, and decision-making across both aerial and ground platforms. However, this interconnectivity also introduces new challenges for anomaly detection, as attacks or cyber intrusions in a single vehicle can propagate through the system, increasing vulnerability. Existing intrusion detection approaches typically focus on CAVs or UAVs in isolation, leaving integrated CAV–UAV systems largely unexplored. In this paper, we propose a machine learning-based methodology for anomaly detection in combined UAV–CAV environments. The framework is architecture-agnostic and data-driven, enabling adaptation to diverse operational scenarios and vehicle types. The proposal incorporates temporal, spatial, and feature-level anomaly detection through attention mechanisms and a dynamic ensemble scheme, enhancing robustness and accuracy. By leveraging vehicle-level decentralized computation, the proposed method supports scalable detection across interconnected aerial and ground vehicles. The proposed approach provides an adaptive, scalable, and cooperative platform for resilient anomaly detection in next-generation integrated UAV–CAV ecosystems, achieving improvements of up to 50%, 40%, and 12% in computational cost, detection delay, and accuracy, respectively.

title: Explainability Boosted Anomaly Detection Framework for O-RAN Based NextG Networks.
abstract: The wireless networks have historically faced significant security vulnerabilities, necessitating advanced anomaly detection mechanisms, especially as networks evolve towards 6G and beyond. This study introduces an advanced anomaly detection framework that leverages explainable artificial intelligence to enhance the security of next-generation (NextG) cellular networks. By implementing and evaluating a variety of artificial intelligence models, the framework demonstrates high accuracy and efficient runtime performance in identifying malicious traffic within a realistic Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) testbed. A key innovation of this work is the integration of post-hoc explainability methods to identify the most critical key performance metrics (KPMs), which enables a significant 80% reduction in dataset complexity without compromising detection accuracy. Additionally, explainability analyses identify several critical attack traffic characteristics, such as protocol type, bandwidth, interval, and duration, to prevent upcoming network attacks. The resulting framework effectively balances computational efficiency, accuracy, and explainability, underscoring its practical applicability for enhancing security in next-generation cellular networks.

title: Improved Data Detection Scheme for Massive MIMO Systems.
abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) serves as a cornerstone technology for beyond fifth-generation$(5 \mathrm{G})$wireless networks, delivering significant improvements in both spectral and energy efficiency. However, one of the key challenges lies in designing signal detection algorithms that achieve high performance while maintaining low computational complexity. Iterative detection techniques have gained significant attention, where they progressively improve the accuracy of detection through a series of successive updates or iterations. In this work, we propose two novel hybrid massive MIMO detectors: the improved Newton method (INI) combined with Gauss-Seidel (GS) and the INI combined with successive overrelaxation (SOR). The motivation behind this work is to combine low-complexity iterative methods with the adaptive and recursive estimation power of INI, resulting in a more efficient and accurate detection process. By first applying a lightweight INI-based initialization and then refining the estimate using efficient iterative updates, the proposed detectors can accelerate convergence with significantly reduced complexity. Simulation results demonstrate superior performance, outperforming existing up-to-date detectors, making them well-suited for practical deployments.

title: CRAFT: A Co-Adaptive Freeze and Train Strategy for Dynamic Neural Networks.
abstract: Dynamic Neural Networks (DyNNs) can adapt their structure or parameters dynamically, making them suitable for wireless communication systems with varying modulation schemes and channel conditions. A key challenge, however, is the large memory overhead of storing separate parameter sets for each modulation order. To address this issue, we present three main contributions. 1) A DyNN-based demodulator that computes log-likelihood ratios for multiple modulation schemes, where higher-order constellations reuse parameters from lowerorder ones via a Co-adaptive Freeze and Train (CRAFT) strategy. 2) A link-level evaluation on a 5G-NR SIMO CDL-C channel, demonstrating a minimal SNR loss (1 dB) for lowerorder modulations, with comparable or improved performance for higher-order constellations relative to a fully flexible DyNN and consistent gains over approximate ML-MAP demodulation. 3) A parameter count and memory analysis in GF$22-\text{nm}$FDSOI CMOS technology, demonstrating a 24% reduction in parameters and up to 28% reduction in area and total power using an 8k SRAM macro compared to a fully flexible DyNN.

title: Resource-Aware Semantic Communication with Adaptive Vision Transformers for Digital Twins.
abstract: In the Metaverse, real-time digital twin (DT) updates enable immersive, interactive environments by reflecting real world states. Metaverse can engage its users to share data in order to ensure the completeness of the DT. However, the limitations and heterogeneity in IoT devices' computation and transmission resources are critical challenges to synchronizing the vast volume of real-world objects with their digital replicas. In this work, we propose a novel adaptive Vision Transformer (ViT)- based semantic communication (SemCom) system to extract semantic information from raw data collected by IoT devices. The system dynamically adjusts the model size and computational complexity according to the resource constraints of individual IoT devices, enables broader participation of heterogeneous devices, enhances feature extraction capabilities, and ensures completeness and efficient DT representation. We formulate our problem as an utility-maximization optimization to manage ViT complexity under resource constraints, allowing the Metaverse Services Provider (MSP) to select high-performing IoT devices. To guide the optimization, we profile ViT models with varying architectural complexities and conduct an empirical analysis to capture the relationship between model scale and performance. To address the scalability and privacy limitations of the optimization, we propose a decentralized solution where each IoT device independently optimizes its own utility under local constraints. The MSP, in turn, selects among these devices to ensure quality and maximize its overall utility. We show that our distributed solution achieves near-optimal performance and significantly outperforms other approaches in terms of MSP utility, semantic data quality, and overall IoT utility. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Performance Evaluation for Deep Learning-Based Signal Detection in Underwater Visible Light Communication.
abstract: Underwater visible light communication (UVLC) has sparked wide research interest for its potential of providing high data-rate services in underwater scenarios. However, UVLC faces significant challenges due to the complicated and unpredictable underwater channel conditions caused by absorption and scattering that vary with different water types. These phenomena make acquiring accurate channel state information (CSI) and reliable signal detection particularly difficult. In this paper, we propose a deep learning (DL)-based approach that combines the channel estimation (CE) and signal detection (SD) processes using long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network. By leveraging the underwater channel characteristics learned through offline training, our DL-based method treats the channel as a black-box and jointly performs CE and SD. Simulation results demonstrate that without prior channel knowledge, the proposed method significantly outperforms the conventional CE approach, i.e., minimum mean square error (MMSE) in terms of bit-error-rate (BER) across varying signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and closely matches with the optimal maximum likelihood (ML) detection that typically requires perfect CSI. This highlights the potential of LSTM in learning the complex underwater environment, and providing robust UVLC signal detection compared to traditional CE technique.

title: Low-Complexity VAMP Detector for Affine Frequency Division Multiplexing Systems.
abstract: Affine Frequency Division Multiplexing (AFDM) has emerged as a promising waveform for high-mobility wireless communications, achieving full delay-Doppler diversity through the discrete affine Fourier transform. This paper presents a computationally efficient detector for AFDM systems using a low-complexity Vector Approximate Message Passing (VAMP) algorithm that employs the conjugate gradient method to solve the linear estimation problem iteratively, eliminating the need for expensive singular value decomposition operations required by standard VAMP algorithms. The proposed approach employs diagonal preconditioning and simultaneous trace estimation to maintain detection accuracy while significantly reducing computational complexity from cubic to quadratic scaling in the number of subcarriers. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed detector achieves bit error rate performance comparable to standard VAMP across multiple modulation schemes while reducing computational burden by factors ranging from five to ten for practical system dimensions, making it highly suitable for real-time implementation in resource-constrained high-mobility communication systems.

title: MIMO-Zak-OTFS with Superimposed Spread Pilots.
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of spread pilot design and effective channel estimation in multiple-input multiple-output Zak-OTFS (MIMO-Zak-OTFS) with superimposed spread pilots, where data and spread pilot signals are superimposed in the same frame. To achieve good estimation performance in a MIMO setting, the spread pilots at different transmit antennas need to be effectively separated at the receiver. Towards this, we propose a spread pilot design that separates the pilot sequences in the cross-ambiguity domain and enables the estimation of the effective channel taps by a simple read-off operation. To further alleviate the effect of pilot-data interference on performance, we carry out turbo iterations between channel estimation and detection. Simulation results for $2\times 2$ and $3\times 3$ MIMO-Zak-OTFS with Gaussian-sinc pulse shaping filter for vehicular-A channel model show that the proposed pilot design and estimation scheme with three turbo iterations can achieve very good estimation/detection performance.

title: Atmospheric Ducts in Wireless Propagation: Analytical and Data-Driven Range Extension Models.
abstract: Tropospheric ducts extend radio links beyond the geometric horizon, significantly impacting terrestrial backhaul and maritime connectivity; however, accurately modeling this phenomenon remains challenging. Widely used approaches, such as parabolic-equation (PE) solvers and ITU-R P.452, are either computationally intensive or rely on limited-fidelity climatological surrogates. We develop a vertical-profile-driven, closed-form model for ducted path loss and range. First, vertical refractivity gradient and duct thickness are mapped to a confinement index that governs an effective spreading model and a bounce-tokilometer attenuation slope combining gas/rain absorption with reflection/leakage. Second, a single analytic loss model is inverted in closed form via the Lambert-$W$function to yield ducted distance, range extension, and duct gain directly from link-budget inputs. Calibration against ITU-R P. 452 via a confinement-to-time-percentage mapping shows monotone scaling, cross-band coherence, and close agreement: RMSE$=14.7 ~\text{km}$and MAE = 13.6 km for ducted-range medians and path-loss curves at 7 GHz track within 1-2 dB across weak/medium/strong ducts. Reliability curves and gain-confinement plots show that ducts provide over 100 km of additional reach, depending on band and confinement.

title: Machine Learning-Based Transceivers: Two-Stage Training for Digital Modulation.
abstract: Recent advances in machine learning have inspired the redesign of fundamental building blocks of wireless communication systems. In this paper, we investigate an end-to-end learning framework for digital modulation using neural networks. We introduce a machine learning (ML)-based transceiver that we name in short “smart transceiver”. For this, we propose a two-stage training process: (i) supervised demodulation training with pilot symbols transmitted by a conventional system, and (ii) modulation training via communication between a learned demodulator and a neural modulator, under additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) conditions. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are employed to learn robust symbol constellations and decoding strategies without relying on explicit channel models. We systematically analyze the impact of training parameters, including the number of training bits, on the learning outcome. Performance is evaluated in terms of bit error rate (BER) and compared against conventional transceivers. Our results demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive performance with a loss of less than 0.5 dB while adapting to channel conditions, highlighting the potential of ML for future communication systems beyond manually engineered constellations.

title: Enabling Green Hybrid Networks with Plasmodesmata-Inspired Molecular Links.
abstract: Molecular communication via diffusion (MCvD) is a bio-inspired paradigm for nanonetworks and sustainable communication systems, enabling nanoscale information transfer where electromagnetic methods are limited. MCvD occurs naturally in biological systems and can take place in both unbounded and bounded environments, often relying on specialized structures that mediate selective transport, such as plasmodesmata (PDs) in plants. Here, we focus on PDs, whose structural simplicity makes them suitable as models for communication frameworks. To address scalability issues of particle-based models in complex tissues, a voxel-based framework for PD-mediated MCvD is introduced, enabling efficient simulations through spatial discretization. Incorporating plasmodesmata-inspired molecular links allows MCvD to integrate into broader network architectures as controllable nanoscale channels bridging molecular, optical, and wireless modalities. This approach supports dense IoT sensing and hybrid networks with wireless systems, while laying the foundation for the Internet of Plants, with applications in crop monitoring, precision agriculture, and bio-hybrid networks for energy-efficient communication inspired by natural intercellular processes.

title: Nonparametric Variational Bayesian Learning for Channel Estimation with OTFS Modulation.
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation has demonstrated significant advantages in high-mobility scenarios in future 6 G networks. However, existing channel estimation methods often overlook the structured sparsity and clustering characteristics inherent in realistic clustered delay line (CDL) channels, leading to degraded performance in practical systems. To address this issue, we propose a novel nonparametric Bayesian learning (NPBL) framework for OTFS channel estimation. Specifically, a stick-breaking process is introduced to automatically infer the number of multipath components and assign each path to its corresponding cluster. The channel coefficients within each cluster are modeled by a Gaussian mixture distribution to capture complex fading statistics. Furthermore, an effective pruning criterion is designed to eliminate spurious multipath components, thereby enhancing estimation accuracy and reducing computational complexity. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance in terms of normalized mean squared error compared to existing methods.

title: A Novel On-Policy Deep Actor-Critic Framework for NOMA-Enabled RIS-Aided Cell-Free mMIMO.
abstract: This paper investigates a non-orthogonal multiple access enabled reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) aided cellfree massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) system by designing optimal RIS beamforming to maximize the achievable throughput, while considering imperfect channel state information and spatial correlation. Most existing studies primarily focus on off-policy deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based RIS phase shifts designing in conventional RIS-assisted cellular systems. However, there is a lack of research in applying on-policy DRL methods for designing optimal RIS phase shifts in a more complex scenario of RISaided CF-mMIMO systems. To address the formulated nonconvex throughput maximization problem, a novel on-policy deep reinforcement learning algorithm is proposed within a Markov decision process framework, namely Enhanced Advantage Actor-Critic (E-A2C). E-A2C offers improved exploration efficiency through its advantage function and multi-worker agent learning structure. Numerical results validate the stability, convergence, and optimality of the proposed E-A2C algorithm. Furthermore, the proposed E-A2C algorithm demonstrates superior throughput performance compared to the baseline schemes.

title: Quantum-Neuromorphic Hybrid Architecture for Energy-Efficient Multi-Agent Coordination in Distributed Healthcare Networks.
abstract: This study introduces a hybrid quantum-neuromorphic computing architecture for multi-agent wireless healthcare networks that must meet strict energy, latency, and reliability requirements. My approach separates global optimization from real-time execution by combining Variational Quantum Circuits (VQCs) for system-wide coordination with Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) running on neuromorphic hardware for ultra-low-power local decision making. To reduce communication overhead, I propose a Quantum-inspired Spike-Timing Protocol (QSTP), which converts a quantum-derived correlation structure into spike-timing patterns that enable event-driven coordination with minimal beaconing. I implemented a VQC-based multi-agent resource allocation method (QC-MARA) and deployed policy execution using STDP-enabled spiking agents. Across a 12-agent Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) under interference and mobility, the proposed system achieves a 78% energy reduction compared with classical deep reinforcement learning while maintaining sub-50 ms end-toend latency and$99.9 {\%}+$packet delivery reliability, supporting safety-critical medical monitoring and long-term operation.

title: CKM Beyond Channel Gain: Spatial Correlation Map Construction with Deep Learning.
abstract: Channel knowledge map (CKM) is a promising technique to achieve environment-aware wireless communication and sensing. Constructing the complete CKM based on channel knowledge observations at sparse locations is a fundamental problem for CKM-enabled wireless networks. However, most existing works on CKM construction only consider the special type of CKM, i.e., the channel gain map (CGM), which only records the channel gain value for each location. In this paper, we consider the channel spatial correlation map (SCM) construction, which signifies the location-specific spatial correlation matrix for multi-antenna systems. Unlike CGM construction, constructing SCM poses significant challenges due to its extremely highdimensional structure. To address this issue, we first decompose the high-dimensional SCM into lower-dimensional path gain map (PGM) and path angle map (PAM). Then we propose a deep learning model termed E-SRResNet for constructing high-quality SCM from sparse samples, which incorporates multi-head attention (MHA) mechanisms and multi-scale feature fusion (MSFF) to accurately model both local and global spatial relationships of channel parameters and complex nonlinear mappings. Furthermore, we preprocess the dataset to provide priors including line-of-sight (LoS) map, binary building map and base station (BS) map for the model to reconstruct SCM more accurately. Simulations conducted on the CKMImageNet dataset demonstrate that the proposed E-SRResNet achieves significant performance improvements over baseline methods. Moreover, the cosine similarity between the constructed SCM and the ground truth exceeds 0.8 in most regions, validating the effectiveness of the proposed construction method.

title: Unified Trellis Design for Realizing Pilot-Symbol-Less Wireless Communications.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a unified trellis-based estimation and detection approach for realizing Pilot-SymbolLess (PSL) wireless communications. We incorporate the prior knowledge to the data symbols and make them become a special art of Reference Signal (RS), i.e. PSL symbols, which is the key design philosophy of PSL communication. PSL communication does not assign dedicated wireless resource for the conventional pilots purpose, and is thus free of the pilot overhead. In order to approach the PSL effect, we can exploit either differential coding to integrate the prior knowledge through Differential Phase Shift Keying (DPSK) based PSL symbols or standard compliant Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM) based PSL symbols. The unified trellis structure will facilitate the joint channel estimation, channel tracking and data detection. Furthermore, we extend the trellis design to support the Multiple-Input MultipleOutput (MIMO) and massive MIMO (mMIMO) systems without introducing exponential increasing of the state nodes in the trellis, which leads to acceptable implementation complexity. Numerical simulations exhibit that mMIMO systems will be benefited from PSL philosophy due to rich spatial diversity, even preferably for medium and high mobility scenarios.

title: Learning Doppler-Resilient Keys via CNN-Based Channel Mapping for UAV Communications.
abstract: Physical layer key generation (PLKG) offers a lightweight and scalable approach to securing wireless communications by exploiting the reciprocity and randomness of the channel. However, in high-mobility scenarios such as unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications, rapid channel variations and reduced coherence time undermine channel reciprocity, significantly degrading the reliability of PLKG. In this work, we propose a Doppler-resilient PLKG framework to improve key generation performance in dynamic wireless environments. We develop a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based model that learns to map the channel frequency response (CFR) observed at the ground control station (GCS) to the corresponding CFR at the UAV. By integrating Doppler frequency and CFR through a feature fusion layer, the framework adapts to varying mobility conditions and enables stable key generation across different Doppler scenarios. A unified model is trained on aggregated datasets to support robust performance without requiring Doppler-specific tuning. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior key consistency and adaptability, significantly reducing the key disagreement rate (KDR) compared with existing deep learning-based approaches across a wide range of Doppler frequencies.

title: Real-Time Pollution Detection for IIoT: A Hybrid Reinforcement Learning Offloading Framework for Multi-Tier Satellite Networks.
abstract: Continuous and real-time pollution detection in industrial environments within the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is crucial for maintaining ecological balance and ensuring the safe operation of industrial facilities. However, traditional pollution detection methods suffer from limitations in coverage and data timeliness. In recent years, the rapid development of satellite remote sensing technology has provided new opportunities to address these challenges. To this end, we propose an edge computing framework integrating satellite remote sensing with IIoT. This approach deploys deep learning models for pollution detection directly on satellites, enabling real-time on-orbit analysis and processing of captured images and downlinking only key detection results (e.g., pollution location, type, and extent), thereby significantly enhancing response speed. We first outline the architecture and processing workflow of this edge computing system, followed by the development of a hybrid Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C) and Decision Transformer (DT) reinforcement learning algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method dynamically optimizes the trade-off between processing accuracy and latency in pollution detection tasks under strict delay constraints, thus meeting the urgent demands for high timeliness and wide coverage in IIoT scenarios.

title: Ultra-Low-Complexity Multigroup Multicast Beamforming in Frame-Based Geo Satellite Communication.
abstract: Multicast transmission have been widely adopted in geosynchronous satellites for resource efficiency. This paper proposes an ultra-low-complexity multigroup multicast beamforming algorithm using nonlinear eigenvalue problem (NEPv) formulation and Lagrange dual decomposition (LDD). Specifically, we formulate a sum rate maximization (SRM) problem under power and quality of service (QoS) constraints. By decoupling the problem, we optimize beam directions via NEPv while reallocating power by LDD to satisfy the constraints. Unlike conventional successive convex approximation (SCA) methods, our approach addresses first-order optimality directly to obtain semi-closedform solutions. Simulations show that the proposed NEPv-LDD performs near-identically to existing SCA-based algorithms while reducing computation time to$0.6 \%-2 \%$.

title: Hybrid Beamforming and Trajectory Optimization for Adaptive Resource Allocation of UAV-enabled ISAC Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we propose an adaptive resource allocation scheme for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, in which communication and sensing resources, including radio frequency (RF) chains and transmit power, are dynamically allocated to meet the varying task requirements in complex environments. Specifically, we first propose an adaptive scheduling mechanism that judiciously determines the ratio of resources allocated for communication. Accordingly, a hybrid beamforming scheme is introduced, where RF resources are allocated by the resource ratio to achieve dynamic communication and sensing resource distribution. Finally, an alternating optimization framework is developed to jointly optimize the UAV trajectory, resource allocation, and beamforming for maximizing the system's communication and sensing performance performance. Simulations validate that the proposed scheme can adaptively adjust the resource allocation strategy to better satisfy communication and sensing performance requirements due to complex environments and dynamic task demands, compared to various benchmarks.

title: GRLP-Based Resource Allocation for Multimodal Semantics and Bit Coexistence Communication in Heterogeneous Vehicle Networks.
abstract: Semantic communications are widely regarded as a key enabling technology for future sixth-generation (6 G) networks. The fundamental idea is to leverage deep neural networks to extract and compress task-relevant semantic information over end-to-end links, thereby significantly enhancing communication efficiency and intelligence. In future vehicular networks, connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs) and human-driven vehicles (HDVs) are expected to coexist for a long period: the former can be equipped with semantic transceivers, while the latter continue to operate with conventional transceivers. To meet the stringent communication requirements of vehicles during critical maneuvers (e.g., lane changes), we proposes a joint resource optimization approach tailored for heterogeneous vehicular networks. Specifically, we jointly optimize the beamforming matrix, power allocation, and the number of semantic symbols to maximize the weighted semantic rate of CAVs and the bit rate of HDVs. Meanwhile, lane-change probabilities are embedded into the objective function to enable resource prioritization for vehicles with potential lane-changing intentions. To this end, we design a framework based graph neural network (GNN) with deep reinforcement learning (DRL), while integrating lane-change prediction(GRLP). In this framework, vehicles are modeled as graph nodes, where a graph aggregation mechanism captures inter-vehicle correlations, and the resulting representations are fed into a reinforcement learning agent to derive optimal resource allocation strategies. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can adaptively configure resource for lane-changing vehicles, while preserving the communication performance of other vehicles, thereby significantly improving link reliability and system throughput.

title: UAV-Enabled Movable Antenna Array Designs for Wireless Communications.
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) equipped with movable antennas demonstrate significant potential for enhancing communication system performance, leveraging their platform mobility and antenna spatial degrees of freedom. To this end, this work proposes a joint optimization framework that aims to maximize the uplink communication rate by cooperatively optimizing the receive beamforming vector, user transmit power, and antenna positioning. Due to the highly coupled and non-convex nature of the problem, an iterative algorithm is developed to efficiently solve it. Simulation results show that the proposed method achieves notable performance improvement compared to the conventional schemes with fixedposition antennas.

title: Topology Semantic Routing in Multi-Layer Satellite Networks.
abstract: Mega-constellations introduce frequent and predictable topological changes due to orbital motion, link dynamics, and weather-affected feeder availability. Classical routing approaches relying on global re-signaling are unable to maintain stable connectivity under such dynamics, leading to increased overhead, delayed convergence, and degraded delivery. In this article, we introduce the topology semantic routing concept that enables space nodes to adapt their forwarding behavior based on local and momentary topology interpretation. Routing protocol signaling is deferred or avoided for transient or expected changes, and path selection is adjusted using time-aligned information or localized failure detection. The mechanism integrates with distributed and centralized frameworks and is suited for homomorphic and cyclic topologies, frequently occurring in mega-constellations. Furthermore, the results of a simulation-based evaluation under orbital shifts, feeder handovers, and link degradation show that time- and event-driven redirect strategies maintain delivery performance and reduce signaling overhead, confirming applicability in dynamic non-terrestrial infrastructures.

title: Beyond Link-Level Enhancements: System-Level Optimizations in AI-Native 6G RANs.
abstract: The increasing complexity of dense 6G RAN environments necessitates a paradigm shift from conventional linklevel optimization toward system-level control mechanisms that ensure intelligent coordination of radio resources, mobility, and device management across multiple coexisting RANs. Traditional optimization techniques, including advanced beamforming, modulation schemes, and interference mitigation, operate within isolated link boundaries, lacking the global awareness necessary for dense deployments. In contrast, system-wide AI-driven control frameworks enable holistic optimization, dynamically adjusting network parameters to adapt to fluctuating demand, user mobility patterns, and energy efficiency constraints. This paper proposes an AI-native system-level RAN control architecture, which redistributes core network functionalities to the edge and introduces a flexible deployment model: as part of C-RAN, as an independent edge core, or within the centralized network infrastructure. The proposed approach enhances power and frequency management, optimizes paging and mobility execution at the edge, and reduces core signaling overhead by executing localized resource coordination and interference control. AI plays a fundamental role in this transition, enabling real-time adaptive decision-making tailored to localized network conditions. By shifting from isolated, link-level improvements to a coordinated, AI-driven system-level optimization paradigm, the proposed framework enables efficient, scalable, and resilient dense RAN deployments. Future work will focus on prototype development and real-world validation, assessing the impact of AI-based RAN management and local mobility execution while ensuring seamless integration with existing 6G network architectures.

title: Hierarchical Deep Learning for Joint Turbulence and PE Estimation in Multi-Aperture FSO Systems.
abstract: Accurate characterization of free-space optical (FSO) channels requires joint estimation of transmitter pointing errors, receiver angle-of-arrival (AoA) fluctuations, and turbulence-induced fading. However, existing literature addresses these impairments in isolation, since their multiplicative coupling in the received signal severely limits conventional estimators and prevents simultaneous recovery. In this paper, we introduce a novel multi-aperture FSO receiver architecture that leverages spatial diversity across a lens array to decouple these intertwined effects. Building on this hardware design, we propose a hierarchical deep learning framework that sequentially estimates AoA, transmitter pointing error, and turbulence coefficients. This decomposition significantly reduces learning complexity and enables robust inference even under strong atmospheric fading. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves near-MAP accuracy with orders-of-magnitude lower computational cost, and substantially outperforms end-to-end learning baselines in terms of estimation accuracy and generalization. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to demonstrate practical joint estimation of these three key parameters, paving the way for reliable, turbulence-resilient multi-aperture FSO systems.

title: Multi-User ISAC Beamforming Considering Hardware Impairments of Linear Power Amplifiers.
abstract: This paper investigates the beamforming design for multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems with hardware imperfections in linear power amplifiers. The Cram'er Rao Bound (CRB) minimization problem is formulated by constraining the power of communication devices and the signalto-noise ratio threshold. Specifically, we first reformulate the CRB using the Schur complement theorem, and then employ semidefinite relaxation to equivalently reconstruct the nonconvex constraints. Subsequently, we obtained the optimal solution using the Gaussian randomization algorithm. Simulation results confirm that the proposed transmission waveform design is more robust when accounting for hardware impairments of linear power amplifiers.

title: Machine-Learning-Based BPSK Decoding Under Fading Channels: A Comparative Study with Maximum Likelihood Detection.
abstract: Machine learning (ML) techniques are increasingly being explored as alternatives to classical detection methods in wireless communication systems, particularly in scenarios involving complex or unknown channel conditions. This paper presents a detailed comparative analysis of several supervised ML classifiers for detecting binary phase shift keying (BPSK) symbols transmitted through representative small scale fading channels, namely Rayleigh, Rician, and Nakagami-m. Five commonly used classifiers like Decision Tree,$k$Nearest Neighbors (k-NN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Gaussian Naive Bayes and Random Forest are evaluated and compared against the optimal single input single output (SISO) maximum likelihood detector (MLD). Monte Carlo simulations are conducted on a wide range of signal to noise ratio (SNR) values from 0 to 20 dB, using instantaneous channel state information (CSI) for both MLD based detection and feature generation for classifier training. The results show that while the SISO MLD continues to provide the theoretical lower bound on the bit error rate (BER), several ML classifiers approach ML performance at moderate to high SNR levels, with Random Forest and SVM demonstrating the strongest consistency across fading environments. The analysis highlights the potential of low complexity ML-based detectors in practical systems and provides insights into classifier robustness, cross channel generalization behavior, and computational trade offs.

title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Resource Slicing for eMBB and URLLC in O-RAN.
abstract: Open radio access networks (O-RAN) enable flexible orchestration of heterogeneous services such as enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB) and ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC), but jointly satisfying their conflicting throughput and latency requirements leads to a highly combinatorial resource allocation problem. In this paper, we propose a hybrid quantum-classical optimization framework for dynamic O-RAN resource slicing, leveraging the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) to jointly optimize radio resource block assignment, punctured scheduling, and power allocation in multi-O-RU networks. The proposed framework integrates orthogonal and shared slicing through a quantumenabled puncturing mechanism that allows URLLC traffic to preempt eMBB transmissions while maintaining overall system efficiency. An adaptive weight normalization strategy driven by real-time queue dynamics balances eMBB throughput maximization and URLLC latency minimization. The resulting constrained optimization problem is mapped to a quantum-executable Hamiltonian and solved using a hybrid QAOA-classical refinement loop compatible with noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices. Simulation results show that the proposed approach outperforms classical optimization baselines, achieving up to 25% higher eMBB throughput, faster convergence, and consistently lower URLLC latency across different power budgets and network densities.

title: Split Channel Based CSI Auto-Encoder for Resource Limited Devices.
abstract: Optimal wireless communication performance relies on aligning transmitted data with the actual channel with the help of precoding matrix, necessitating accurate downlink (DL) channel state information (CSI) at the network (NW). Existing solutions either use codebook-based techniques by exploiting sparsity in spatial or temporal domains, or AI/ML models to compress CSI feedback, but these suffer from high complexity for relatively low-end user equipment (UE) and require multiple models to support several Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) configurations. To address this, we propose a single neural network (NN) based auto-encoder (AE) framework compatible with all MIMO setups through a novel pre/post-processing technique. By training the model on individual 1 × 1 subchannels, we achieve lower complexity, while eliminating the need for configuration-specific models thus reducing UE storage demands significantly. Through mathematical modelling and extensive simulations, we show that with proposed method of using split channel matrix in comparison to full channel matrix as input for NN model, memory requirement for storing model for 4 × 4 MIMO configuration at UE and NW is reduced by 93.58%, with improvement in model performance on high correlation test data by 5.76 dB is observed.

title: Performance Characterization of Pinching-Antenna System with Movable Waveguides.
abstract: This paper proposes a movable waveguide (MW)-enabled pinching-antenna system (PASS), in which each waveguide is connected via a flexible cable and can be linearly moved by drivers. By simultaneously moving the MWs and the pinching antennas (PAs) on them, MW-enabled PASS can effectively track user locations and form flexible array geometries for efficient beamforming. We consider a multi-user downlink communication scenario and derive an upper bound on the minimum rate among all users. To maximize their minimum rate, we propose a low-complexity two-scale optimization algorithm, where the large-scale global search coarsely determines the MW and PA positions, followed by a small-scale local search to finely tune them. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves performance close to the derived bound and can flexibly adapt to different user distributions compared with the conventional PASS employing dense or sparse fixed-position waveguides (FPWs).

title: DRL-Based Multi-AUVs Cooperative Path Planning Under Acoustic Field Constraint.
abstract: Employing autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) for ocean observation and data collection holds great promise for building large-scale underwater monitoring networks. Path planning is a key technique for improving multi-AUVs cooperative efficiency; however, it faces significant challenges from unknown obstacles and highly heterogeneous underwater acoustic fields. In this article, we consider AUVs coordinating environmental sensing during travel to designated target locations. This approach maximizes platform utilization. In particular, we use ray-tracing to construct a three-dimensional acoustic transmission model. We propose a cooperative path planning scheme integrating acoustic field alignment (AFA) and collision-avoidance constraints. The scheme shortens trajectory length and enhances network throughput. Furthermore, to address this challenging dynamic planning problem, we design an energy- and acoustic-aware dueling deep$Q$network (EA-DuelingDQN) that incorporates a recurrent neural network (RNN) module to capture the temporal characteristics of sensing data. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior collision-avoidance capability and network throughput, with the task completion rate improving by 40% compared to conventional DQN-based approaches.

title: Q-Sentinel: Towards Adversarial Robustness for Quantum-Classical xApps in Intelligent O-RAN.
abstract: As Open radio access networks(O-RAN) shifts toward microservice-based disaggregation, learning-enabled xApps now shoulder near-real-time tasks such as interference classification that must react within tens of milliseconds. Hybrid quantum-classical models are a potential fit for that workload because expressive quantum feature maps can be paired with lightweight classical heads to deliver low-latency, energy-efficient inference as the hardware matures. Yet the same variational circuits remain vulnerable to RF adversaries: input perturbations collapses the quantum decision boundary, while parameter-space attacks silently corrupt circuit weights. We present$Q$-Sentinel, a quantum-fidelity aware robust stack that unifies (i) quantum state transformation guided by trusted manifolds, (ii) fidelity-based decision-boundary reinforcement, and (iii) sentinel snapshots that monitor cosine drift and trigger auto-repair of the variational (fusion-inclusive) parameters. We also build a quantum-aware adversarial training (QAT) baseline that applies QC-FGSM/PGD to both spectrogram inputs and quantum encodings. Evaluating with the public dataset SOI-vs-CWI, Q-Sentinel sustains 98.2 % clean accuracy, raises worst-case QC-FGSM/QC-PGD accuracy to 84.7 % / 73.6 % at$\epsilon=0.1$, and retains 70.8 % accuracy under QCPoison while capping mean parameter drift at$1.8 \times 10^{-2}$less than half that of the undefended model. These results indicate that future quantum-assisted O-RAN deployments will require defenses that preserve quantum-state geometry on Hilbert manifolds and continuously repair compromised circuits, extending beyond input-only adversarial training.

title: Duality-Based Fixed Point Iteration Algorithm for Beamforming Design in ISAC Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the beamforming design problem in an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where a multi-antenna base station simultaneously serves multiple communication users while performing radar sensing. We formulate the problem as the minimization of the total transmit power, subject to signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints for communication users and mean-squarederror (MSE) constraints for radar sensing. The core challenge arises from the complex coupling between communication SINR requirements and sensing performance metrics. To efficiently address this challenge, we first establish the equivalence between the original ISAC beamforming problem and its semidefinite relaxation (SDR), derive its Lagrangian dual formulation, and further reformulate it as a generalized downlink beamforming (GDB) problem with potentially indefinite weighting matrices. Compared to the classical DB problem, the presence of indefinite weighting matrices in the GDB problem introduces substantial analytical and computational challenges. Our key technical contributions include (i) a necessary and sufficient condition for the boundedness of the GDB problem, and (ii) a tailored efficient fixed point iteration (FPI) algorithm with a provable convergence guarantee for solving the GDB problem. Building upon these results, we develop a duality-based fixed point iteration (Dual-FPI) algorithm, which integrates an outer subgradient ascent loop with an inner FPI loop. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed Dual-FPI algorithm achieves globally optimal solutions while significantly reducing computational complexity compared with existing baseline approaches.

title: Intelligent Trajectory Design for Free-Space Optical Assisted UAVs Relay Communications in Low-Altitude Airspace.
abstract: With the booming development of low-altitude intelligent networking (LAIN), free-space optical (FSO) based unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) communication offers a promising scheme to effectively address the challenge of the intense spectrum scarcity. However, due to the characteristics of FSO propagation, its performance is severely affected by the lowaltitude atmospheric conditions and complex airspace environment. To address these challenges, this work constructs an FSO assisted UAVs multi-hop relay system, where a multiagent double deep Q-network with prioritized experience replay (MADDQN-PER) approach is proposed for trajectory design, under the complex environment of low-altitude airspace such as the low-altitude obstacles and atmospheric visibility. To expound, the proposed scheme is expected to enhance the relay system capacity by intelligently adjusting UAVs' trajectories in the low-altitude airspace to maintain the multi-hop link stability. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme can effectively avoid time-varying low-altitude threat of varying severity while attaining about 10 % higher capacity when scaling from three to four UAVs.

title: A Dynamic Occupancy Matrix Approach for VANET Routing Using Optimized TD-ISAC.
abstract: The dynamic topologies and high mobility in Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks (VANETs) lead to significant delays and substantial routing overhead, critically undermining safety by restricting real-time message exchange. Autonomous vehicles equipped with advanced sensors (e.g., LiDAR, radar) capture detailed environmental data, yet this capability remains underutilized for network-level optimization. This paper proposes a segmentation-based routing framework that leverages sensorderived vehicle positions to create a dynamic occupancy matrix, a shared topology representation disseminated via a Time Division Integrated Sensing and Communication (TD-ISAC) frame structure inspired by 5G Sidelink. We optimize sensing and communication slots allocation using a hybrid Lagrangian Relaxation and Branch-and-Bound approach to balance topological freshness with communication throughput. The protocol's robustness is further enhanced by a reserve relay mechanism. Simulation results using the Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO) demonstrate that our framework outperforms the Zone Routing Protocol (ZRP) and the Ad-hoc On-demand Distance Vector (AODV) protocol, achieving up to 60 % reduction in end-to-end delay and 5 % reduction in routing overhead in multi-hop scenarios.

title: Pinching Antenna System (PASS) Assisted Wireless Power Transfer (WPT).
abstract: A novel pinching antenna system (PASS)-assisted wireless power transfer (WPT) framework is proposed, where an energy harvesting receiver (EHR) and an information decoding receiver (IDR) coexist. By activating pinching antennas (PAs) in the vicinity of both receivers and flexibly adjusting the PAs' power radiation ratios, the proposed framework is able to simultaneously enhance the energy harvesting efficiency and the communication quality. To tackle the strong coupling among variables, a bilevel optimization problem is formulated. Specifically, the upper level maximizes the power conversion efficiency (PCE) by jointly optimizing the transmit beamforming, PA positions, and the feasible interval of the power radiation ratio under the IDR's rate requirement, while the lower level refines the power radiation ratio within the obtained interval to maximize the achievable sum rate. Efficient solution methods are developed for the two-user case by leveraging alternating optimization (AO) and weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) techniques, yielding stationary solutions for the coupled design variables. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed PASS-WPT scheme substantially outperforms conventional MIMO and the conventional PASS with fixed power radiation in terms of both PCE and sum rate.

title: Peak Structure Analysis Based Phase-Optimized Precoding for PAPR Reduction in OTFS Systems.
abstract: Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) modulation offers superior performance for high-speed mobility wireless communications but suffers from high Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR), degrading power amplifier efficiency. While PAPR reduction techniques exist for OFDM systems, their application to OTFS remains challenging. This paper proposes a novel PAPR suppression method based on peak structure analysis in the time-frequency domain. By precisely locating time-domain peak structures and establishing an analytical framework for energy concentration regions, our approach guides phase optimization in precoding matrices. The method employs gradient-based finetuning with derived upper bound conditions for phase adjustment parameters and Hadamard multiplication precoding to avoid nonlinear distortion. Simulation results demonstrate over 7.6dB PAPR reduction for 16QAM/64*64 OTFS configurations while maintaining stable bit error rate performance, validating the method's effectiveness for practical high-performance communication systems.

title: AgentWiFi: An Agentic-AI-Enabled Framework for Wi-Fi Cross Layer Optimization.
abstract: Agentic AI systems, supporting complex goal decomposition and effective collaboration among a large number of specialized AI agents, are promising to facilitate the management and performance enhancement of wireless communication networking systems. In this paper, we investigate the potential of agentic AI in future Wi-Fi networks, exploiting its capabilities to address key challenges in current Wi-Fi optimization, including the large-scale parameter configuration across physical and medium access control layers in the IEEE 802.11 standard family, personalized quality-of-experience requirements, and dynamic and diversified physical environments. We propose AgentWiFi, a novel semantic-aware agentic-AI-enabled architecture for crosslayer Wi-Fi network optimization. AgentWiFi can infer users' semantic goals, automatically decompose them into several subtasks, and invoke specialized agents associated with physical, medium access control, and application layers of the Wi-Fi network to fulfill the target goal. Furthermore, we develop a hardware prototype, where open-source large language modelbased agents are implemented and interacted with different layers, and conduct case studies in two representative scenarios of high-data-rate demanding ultra high definition live streaming and low-latency demanding online interactive gaming. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of AgentWiFi in improving Wi-Fi network performance via autonomous cross-layer parameter adjustments. Future directions for agentic AI for Wi-Fi are also discussed.

title: Semantic Knowledge Base-Enhanced Joint Source-Channel Coding Framework for Robust Semantic Communications.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a semantic knowledge base (SKB)-enhanced joint source-channel coding (JSCC) framework, named SKB-JSCC. This framework splits semantic features into two transmission branches with dynamically configurable split ratio, a JSCC-based branch that provides superior performance at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and an SKB-based branch that strengthens robustness at low SNR. Additionally, we introduce a bidirectional gated mutual errorcorrection (BGMEC) module at the receiver and provide theoretical analysis supporting its soundness and effectiveness. The BGMEC module uses cross attention to learn semantic associations between the two branches of streams and treats one stream as conditional information for the other to realize mutual correction and feature fusion. Experimental results illustrate that the BGMEC module provides performance gains for SKB-JSCC over the entire SNR range. Compared with a JSCC-based baseline, SKB-JSCC achieves a 14.3% improvement in transmission performance at low SNR and effectively mitigates the “cliff effect” relative to traditional separation-based schemes.

title: Dual-Polarized Wavenumber-Division Multiplexing in LoS Holographic MIMO Communications with Arbitrary Position and Orientation.
abstract: This paper studies the dual-polarized wavenumber-division multiplexing (WDM) in line-of-sight holographic multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications with the receive surface located in arbitrary position and orientation. Specifically, the dual-polarized MIMO channel is first derived with arbitrary placement of the uniform planar surface at the receiver. Moreover, the radiation pattern of single-mode electric field, the co- and cross-polarization levels, and the channel capacity are analyzed, with emphasis on the impact of the azimuth and elevation angles of the receive surface. Finally, the superior performance of the dual-polarized WDM is verified in terms of the downlink sum-rate of several typical transceiver schemes, offering a viable solution for building future high-rate and flexibly-deployed wireless communication systems.

title: Ring Bayes Near-Field Channel Learning for mmWave Hybrid MIMO Systems Employing Uniform Circular Array.
abstract: This work conceives a Ring-Bayes channel learning framework that unifies Bayesian learning with near-field channel estimation in millimeter-wave (mmWave) hybrid MIMO systems. We develop a near-field channel model with a uniform circular array (UCA) at the base station (BS) and a uniform linear array (ULA) at the user equipment (UE), explicitly accounting for spherical wavefront propagation. Exploiting the inherent sparsity of mmWave channels in the joint angular-distance domain, we construct a structured sparse representation and employ framewise processing to enhance the reliability of multi-antenna UE estimation. Furthermore, we design a concentric-ring codebook tailored to the UCA geometry, which efficiently captures nearfield channel features across both angular and distance domains. Leveraging this structure, the proposed Ring-Bayes framework achieves highly accurate recovery of UCA near-field channels. Extensive simulations demonstrate significant performance gains over existing approaches, establishing Ring-Bayes as a scalable and powerful solution for next-generation mmWave communications.

title: Hybrid AI-Quantum Model with Attention-Guided Variational Circuits for MSSQL Attack Detection in Wireless Networks.
abstract: The increasing prevalence of application-layer attacks, such as MSSQL injection, presents serious security challenges for modern wireless networks. Traditional deep learning-based intrusion detection systems often exhibit high model complexity and limited ability to capture complex feature interactions under imbalanced traffic conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes a hybrid AI-quantum framework with attention-guided variational quantum circuits for MSSQL attack detection. Network traffic features from the CIC-DDoS2019 dataset are embedded and optimized using the Tunicate Swarm Algorithm, followed by convolutional learning to model local dependencies. A variational quantum circuit with learnable rotation and entanglement parameters captures higher-order feature interactions. Experimental results demonstrate an accuracy of 99.99%, with precision, recall, and F1-score all exceeding 99.99%. Ablation analysis further confirms improved parameter efficiency, highlighting the suitability of the proposed approach for secure and sustainable wireless systems.

title: Channel Estimation Performance Analysis for RIS-Aided Cell-Free Massive MIMO with RF Impairments in Secure Communications.
abstract: In this article, we investigate the normalized mean square error (NMSE) performance of channel estimation in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems under radio frequency (RF) impairments and physical layer security constraints. Primarily, the entire channel estimation phase is formulated for both least squares (LS) and minimum mean square error (MMSE) methods, based on a practical cascaded channel model including RIS reflection and hardware distortion. To evaluate estimation accuracy, the NMSE metric is analyzed in closed-form. Specifically, its expectation is derived using largescale system analysis, revealing dependencies on the number of access point antennas$M$, the Ricean$K$-factor, and the pilot power. Then, asymptotic behavior of NMSE is characterized as$M$and$K$tend to infinity. It is shown that the estimation error decreases and then saturates as$M$increases, while it increases and then saturates as$K$becomes large. Furthermore, we explore the impact of pilot power allocation, and demonstrate that MMSE estimation allows for reduced pilot power without severe performance loss. Finally, all theoretical findings are verified through extensive simulations, confirming the effectiveness of our proposed analysis.

title: Robust Beamforming for Digital Twin-Enabled RIS Systems: A Hierarchical Meta-Learning Approach.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) have emerged as a promising technology for enhancing wireless system performance, yet their deployment is constrained by the difficulty of acquiring accurate channel state information (CSI). Digital twin (DT) models provide useful prior information on channel characteristics, but the unavoidable sim-to-real gap caused by modeling inaccuracies and environmental mismatches can substantially degrade performance. To address this limitation, we propose an error-aware hierarchical learning framework, termed GMML-BO, which integrates a statistical channel error model with robust optimization. Distinguished from static uncertainty models, the physical channel realization is expressed as a DTderived estimate superimposed with a stochastic residual whose covariance is recursively updated to capture time-varying sim-to-real mismatches. This formulation enables an error-aware data augmentation scheme and yields a robust empirical risk minimization problem. The problem is solved through a hierarchical architecture: an inner gradient-based manifold metalearning (GMML) core leverages objective-function gradients for real-time adaptation, while an outer Bayesian Optimization (BO) controller autonomously tunes hyperparameters on a slower timescale, ensuring low-latency inference with robust generalization. Simulation results demonstrate that GMML-BO consistently outperforms conventional baselines, exhibits stable convergence, and approaches the performance bound under perfect CSI.

title: Multiplicative Updates Beamforming Design for Hybrid Fully-Connected Millimeter-Wave MIMO Systems.
abstract: Achieving the optimal design of analog and digital beamformers, provided by a hybrid architecture using phase shifters (PSs), is crucial for ensuring the spectral efficiency (SE) of millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication systems. To tackle the challenge of finding optimal hybrid beamformers that directly maximize SE, several studies have adopted the matrix factorization problem as a viable solution in designing at each transceiver side. However, the unit constant modulus (UCM) constraints on analog beamformers resulting from PSs and the joint optimization of digital and analog parts render the hybrid beamforming design problem highly non-convex. In this paper, we develop a hybrid algorithm via the multiplicative update rules technique for solving the matrix factorization problem of finding optimal analog and digital beamformers by easily taking into account practical constraints. By removing the nonnegativity constraints, the proposed method achieves optimal analog and digital beamformers in the hybrid fully connected mmWave multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) architecture through a simple implementation enabled by simultaneous updates offered from the closed-form of the multiplicative update rules. According to the numerical simulations, the proposed design is more effective than state-of-the-art design algorithms and is less complex.

title: Contextual Thompson Sampling for Airborne RIS in mmWave-Enabled Metaverse Networks.
abstract: Current millimeter-wave (mmWave) wireless technology suffers from restricted coverage and inconsistent signal intensity due to tight line-of-sight (LoS) connectivity constraints. Hence, two cutting-edge technologies, aerials and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), overcome these limitations in mmWave-empowered Metaverse networks. We envision deploying an airborne RIS model to support the mmWave base station (mWBS) in highly dense traffic metaverse hotspots (MVHSs) where mWBS or Metaverse users (MVUs) experience complex propagation and non-LoS environment to deliver metaverse services. Yet commercial aerials suffer from limited battery lifetime. Therefore, the path planning of the airborne-RIS should be optimized to support multiple MVHSs simultaneously while accounting for its energy expenditure within mWBS coverage bounds. Hence, we convey this problem as a contextual multiarmed bandit (CMAB) and envision a contextual Thompson sampling (CTS) algorithm to address it effectively. We treat the airborne RIS as the bandit gamer. It serves different MVHSs (bandit arms) in its trajectory to optimize its achievable rate (i.e., the reward). The context vector includes the location of MVHSs, provided via a GPS service, and the payoff history of each MVHS. Extensive simulations confirm the superiority of our envisioned CTS scheme over baseline solutions.

title: Denoising-Enabled Semantic Communication for Robust Earth Observation in 6G Satellite Networks: A Swin Transformer Approach.
abstract: Non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) in 6G enable persistent Earth observation (EO), yet satellite downlinks remain bandwidth-limited and vulnerable to path loss, Doppler, and smallscale fading. We propose a semantic communication (SC) pipeline for satellite EO that deploys a lightweight Swin Transformer encoder onboard and a Swin-based decoder with an optional plug-and-play denoiser at the gateway. Training uses channeldiverse pairs of the same scene to promote channel-invariant representations, while inference operates on a single image for reliability and low latency. Across representative operating points, the gateway denoiser consistently improves reconstruction quality while keeping the transmitted feature budget unchanged. On average, it recovers about 60% of the gap in peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and roughly 25% of the gap in multi-scale structural similarity index (MS-SSIM) relative to a higher-bit-rate baseline. These results show that relocating refinement to the gateway shifts the communication-computation balance toward lower downlink load at comparable quality.

title: Stgread: a Graph Diffusion-Based Approach for Satellite Network Traffic Prediction.
abstract: Satellite networks generate highly dynamic traffic due to frequent topology changes and diverse service demands, making long-horizon forecasting challenging. Existing spatiotemporal graph neural networks (STGNNs) rely on discrete diffusion layers that suffer from oversmoothing and accuracy degradation with depth. We propose STGREAD, a spatiotemporal model integrating reaction-diffusion dynamics with neural ordinary differential equation (ODE) solvers. Each block performs continuous-time propagation with adaptive reaction terms, preserving feature diversity and improving stability. Experiments on large-scale satellite traffic datasets show that STGREAD consistently outperforms baselines including STGCN, DCRNN, Graph WaveNet, and MTGNN. With only two blocks, it achieves a test MSE of 0.1718, reducing error by 9.6% vs. STGCN and 14.5% vs. DCRNN. Even under 200-s horizons, STGREAD maintains 0.187, while baselines exceed 0.19. Dirichlet energy analysis further shows that STGREAD preserves higher feature variance and robustness against oversmoothing, achieving strong accuracy with shallow architectures for dynamic, delay-sensitive satellite networks.

title: A Mixture-of-Generative-Experts Framework for Adaptive Security in Diverse Wireless Environments.
abstract: The future 6 G wireless networks are expected to provide reliable and secure service provisioning in diverse wireless environments, yet the existing studies are mostly based on the underlying assumption of single static wireless scenario. To fill this gap, this paper investigates the physical layer security issue aiming to cover over a variety of wireless scenarios. Specifically, we first establish a model to characterize a set of wireless scenarios and formulate the corresponding physical layer security beamforming problem. Then, we select a few representative scenarios and construct a dedicate generative diffusion model (GDM) for security beamformer output, over which a mixture-of-experts (MoE) framework is established with GDM-based experts. Within the MoE framework, a gating network is trained to recognize the properties of the scenario based on the feature engineering of the channel matrix. The top-rated experts matching the scenario are selected, where the output from the experts are combined as the security beamformer for the scenario. Simulation results show that the proposed MoE framework can accurately identify the scenario with matched experts, and combined experts provide effective security solution for unseen wireless scenarios.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Joint Optimization for UAV-Mounted STAR-RIS Networks with Energy Harvesting.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) are increasingly recognized as an enabling component of sixthgeneration (6 G) wireless systems, as they allow controllable modification of the propagation environment to improve both sum-rate and energy efficiency. This work investigates a UAVmounted simultaneous transmitting and reflecting RIS (STARRIS) network, where an energy-harvesting-enabled aerial platform functions as a reconfigurable relay to support users located on both the reflection and transmission sides. A joint nonconvex optimization problem is formulated to optimize the UAV trajectory, base station beamforming, STAR-RIS reflection and transmission coefficients, and the energy harvesting powersplitting ratio. The objective is to maximize a weighted sum of energy efficiency and harvested energy while satisfying users' quality-of-service (QoS) requirements under practical mobility and transmit power constraints. To address this challenging control problem, deterministic policy-gradient-based deep reinforcement learning algorithms, namely deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) and twin delayed DDPG (TD3), are employed within a continuous-control environment that incorporates realistic Rician fading channels. Simulation results demonstrate that TD3 achieves more stable convergence behavior and superior energy efficiency compared to the baseline DDPG approach while effectively optimizing the weighted objective of energy efficiency and harvested energy.

title: Soft Information Aided Diagonal Kalman Filter for Joint Channel Estimation and Detection in Massive MIMO Systems.
abstract: This paper proposes a soft-information-aided diagonal Kalman filter (SIA-DKF) for joint channel estimation and symbol detection (JED) in massive multipleinput multiple-output (MIMO) systems. Specifically, building upon the Kalman filter (KF) framework for JED, the proposed SIA-DKF incorporates the symbol means and variances obtained from variational inference (VI) into the KF, improving its ability to track channels and mitigating mismatches in the update step. Furthermore, SIA-DKF not only exploits favorable propagation in massive MIMO to simplify the VI for symbol detection, but also employs a diagonal approximation of the covariance matrix at each channel update step, thereby significantly reducing the computational complexity. Simulations confirm that SIA-DKF improves the bit error rate (BER) with lower complexity.

title: Robust Task-Oriented Semantic Communication with Visual-Brain Multimodal Learning.
abstract: Task-oriented semantic communication has gained popularity for its ability to reduce communication overhead without compromising task performance. Semantic-level perturbations pose a critical challenge to task-oriented communication by corrupting task-relevant information. We observe that electroencephalography (EEG) is inherently robust to this type of semantic perturbations, offering a promising avenue for model regularization. To address this problem, we introduce an EEGassisted visual-brain multimodal learning framework, leveraging EEG signals as a proxy for human semantic understanding in training to regularize the image encoder to perturbationrobust semantic representations. Specifically, our framework incorporates two key components: a dual-path learning strategy that balances robustness with task-specific accuracy, and a multipositive InfoNCE loss designed to capture deeper semantic associations between modalities. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior robustness against varying levels of semantic perturbations while maintaining stable performance on clean data.

title: A Safety-Constrained Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reliable Wireless Autonomy.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and reinforcement learning (RL) have shown significant promise in wireless systems, enabling dynamic spectrum allocation, traffic management, and large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) coordination. However, their deployment in mission-critical applications introduces the risk of unsafe emergent behaviors, such as UAV collisions, denial-ofservice events, or instability in vehicular networks. Existing safety mechanisms are predominantly reactive, relying on anomaly detection or fallback controllers that intervene only after unsafe actions occur, which cannot guarantee reliability in ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) settings. In this work, we propose a proactive safety-constrained RL framework that integrates proof-carrying control (PCC) with empowermentbudgeted (EB) enforcement. Each agent action is verified through lightweight mathematical certificates to ensure compliance with interference constraints, while empowerment budgets regulate the frequency of safety overrides to balance safety and autonomy. We implement this framework on a wireless uplink scheduling task using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed PCC+EB controller eliminates unsafe transmissions while preserving system throughput and predictable autonomy. Compared with unconstrained and reactive baselines, our method achieves provable safety guarantees with minimal performance degradation. These results highlight the potential of proactive safety constrained RL to enable trustworthy wireless autonomy in future 6 G networks.

title: Synthetic Cellular Network Modeling via Public Data and AI-Enhanced KPI Modeling.
abstract: Cellular network design, optimization, and performance benchmarking have traditionally depended on proprietary datasets collected by mobile network operators (MNOs), constraining independent research and limiting replicability. This paper introduces an operator-agnostic modeling framework for synthetic cellular network planning and Key Performance Indicator (KPI) generation using openly accessible geospatial and demographic datasets. The framework integrates land use/land cover (LULC) data, population density grids, and publicly available LTE drive-test traces to characterize radio environments without operator intervention. A hybrid statistical-generative modeling pipeline is developed, combining geo-statistical clustering with deep generative AI models to synthesize realistic traffic loads, interference patterns, and KPI distributions across heterogeneous regions. Frequency, bandwidth, and deployment parameters are user-configurable, enabling scenario generalization and transferability across geographic domains. Furthermore, a domain-adaptive learning module enables the trained model to extrapolate KPI behavior in previously unseen environments, achieving operator-level fidelity in coverage, throughput, and quality-of-service metrics. The proposed approach establishes a data-independent methodology for cellular network emulation, promoting reproducibility, cost-efficiency, and open benchmarking. This work highlights how AI-driven surrogate modeling and open geospatial intelligence can democratize access to network performance analytics, accelerating innovation in wireless communication research, digital infrastructure planning, and policymaking.

title: Joint Beamforming and RIS Phase Optimization for Secure HAPS Downlink Communications.
abstract: High altitude platform stations (HAPS) are envisioned as key non-terrestrial base stations in future sixthgeneration (6 G) networks, yet their broadcast links are inherently vulnerable to eavesdropping. This paper investigates the physical layer security (PLS) of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided HAPS downlink communication, where a multiantenna HAPS base station (BS) serves a single antenna ground user in the presence of a single antenna aerial eavesdropper. We formulate the joint design of the HAPS transmit beamformer and phase RIS matrix as a non-convex secrecy rate maximization problem under unit-norm and unit-modulus constraints. An alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is developed for (i) fixed RIS phases, where the secrecy ratio is cast as a generalized Rayleigh quotient, and the optimal beamformer is obtained from the dominant generalized eigenvector, and (ii) for fixed beamformer, RIS phases are refined via element-wise coordinate descent over a finite phase set. To rigorously validate the framework, a small discrete codebook is constructed, and the proposed algorithm is compared against true exhaustive and random optimization (RO). Monte Carlo simulations under realistic HAPS geometries show that the proposed scheme closely approaches exhaustive search while significantly outperforming RO, providing practical insights for secure RIS-aided HAPS deployments.
