title: Edge IoBNT Networks for Bioprocess Digital Twins: A Physics-Informed ML Approach.
abstract: Edge computing is becoming critical for real-time bioprocess monitoring and digital twin (DT) development, which enables low-latency data acquisition and localized intelligence. In biotechnology, wastewater treatment, pharmaceuticals, and healthcare, continuous monitoring of microbial growth requires near-sensor computation and reliable nano-scale communication. Conventional Internet of Things (IoT) frameworks and standard neural networks often lack the network efficiency and physics-awareness needed for precise, adaptive prediction. This paper proposes an Edge framework combining Monod kinetics, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), and the Internet of Bio-Nano Things (IoBNT) to enhance DTs for bioprocess applications. The IoBNT layer enables real-time biochemical sensing through nano-sensors, while PINNs ensure accurate predictions under sparse measurements. Results show 68 % data reduction, latency improved from 24.7 ms to 8.4 ms, PDR increased from 93.5 % to 99.3 %, bandwidth reduced from 11.2 Mbps to 6.8 Mbps, and energy per node decreased from 13.7 mJ to 6.3 mJ, confirming the framework's high efficiency and precision.

title: Design and Optimization of DGS-Based MIMO Antenna Using Machine Learning for Modern Wireless Communications.
abstract: This paper presents the design and machine learning (ML) optimization of a two-port MIMO antenna with a Defected Ground Structure (DGS) for modern wireless communications. The overall dimensions of the proposed MIMO antenna are 90$\text{mm} \times 40 ~\text{mm} \times 0.8 ~\text{mm}$on a Rogers RT duroid 5880 substrate. The results of the MIMO antenna give better isolation (20 dB) and a maximum gain of 2.65 dB with efficiency ($>90 \%$). DGS is used to achieve a resonance frequency of 2.57 GHz over a frequency range. The DGS functions work as a reflector, reducing unwanted radiation. As a result, good isolation in the resonant band is extended. The MIMO design's bandwidth ranges from 2.33 to 2.80 GHz with an impedance bandwidth of 0.47 GHz, a center frequency of 2.565 GHz, and a fractional bandwidth of$\mathbf{1 8. 3 3 \%}$. MIMO diversity performance measures, including ECC ($<0.1$), DG ($>9.95 ~\text{dB}$), MEG (1), TARC ($<-10 ~\text{dB}$), and characteristic results such as S-parameters and radiation patterns, are satisfied and yield better diversity performance. A 2.57 GHz resonance frequency is used for various wireless communication applications, including LTE, Wi-Fi, WLAN, and WiMAX, wearable technology, IoT devices, and some other wireless devices operating in the sub- 6 GHz range. MIMO is optimized using KBNN, ANN, decision trees, and random forest ML methods. The ML optimization approach is used to determine the optimal design parameters for the MIMO. Random forest techniques outperform other ML algorithms in accurately predicting S-parameter S11 (99%).

title: Model-Driven Aided Expectation Propagation Learning for AFDM Signal Detection in High-Mobility Communications.
abstract: In this paper, a deep learning-based Expectation Propagation (EP) algorithm model combined with a Graph Neural Network (GNN) detector (DeepEP-AFDM) is proposed for reliable symbol detection in affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) systems over doubly dispersive channels. The proposed method unfolds the iterative EP algorithm into a deep neural network, preserving the interpretable factor-graph structure while utilizing specialized neural modules to learn adaptive priors and layer-wise damping factors from data. This hybrid design effectively mitigates the severe inter-symbol interference and model mismatch inherent in dense effective AFDM channels, ensuring robust signal recovery in high-mobility scenarios. Simulation results demonstrate that DeepEP-AFDM achieves superior error rate performance compared to the classic EP benchmark, while maintaining a computational complexity order of$\mathcal{O}\left(L N^{2}\right)$comparable to standard EP.

title: Transmission Protocols for Uplink Pinching Antenna Systems (PASS)-Enhanced Sensing.
abstract: Two types of uplink sensing protocols for pinchingantenna systems (PASS)-assisted sensing are proposed in this paper: i) pinch switching (PS), which performs separate pinching beamforming for each time slot, and ii) pinch multiplexing (PM), which applies a single pinching beamforming for all time slots. Instead of using the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) as a sensing performance metric, Bayesian CRB (BCRB) is employed in this paper, which leverages the prior distributions of the sensing parameters, avoiding evaluation at a specific parameter realization. Based on these protocols, both the total power minimization problem subject to a BCRB threshold and the minmax BCRB problem subject to a total power constraint are formulated. By leveraging Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions, these problems are equivalently converted into a search over pinching antenna (PA) positions and solved using an elementwise algorithm. Numerical results show the benefits of PASS over conventional benchmarks and heuristic PA-position-optimization methods for uplink sensing.

title: One-Step Generative Channel Estimation via Average Velocity Field.
abstract: Generative models have shown immense potential for wireless communication by learning complex channel data distributions. However, the iterative denoising process associated with these models imposes a significant challenge in latency-sensitive wireless communication scenarios, particularly in channel estimation. To address this challenge, we propose a novel solution for one-step generative channel estimation. Our approach bypasses the time-consuming iterative steps of conventional models by directly learning the average velocity field. Through extensive simulations, we validate the effectiveness of our proposed method over existing state-of-the-art diffusion-based approach. Specifically, our scheme achieves a normalized mean squared error up to 2.65 dB lower than the diffusion method and reduces latency by around 90%, demonstrating the potential of our method to enhance channel estimation performance.

title: Efficient Beamforming for Discrete SIM-Aided Multiuser Systems Under Statistical CSI.
abstract: Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces (SIM) have emerged as a revolutionary architecture for next-generation wireless communications, offering wave-domain signal processing capabilities with significantly reduced hardware complexity compared to conventional systems. However, most existing SIM research assumes continuous phase shifts and perfect instantaneous channel state information (CSI), which are impractical due to hardware discrete phase shift constraints and prohibitive pilot overhead. This paper presents a joint power allocation and discrete phase shift optimization framework for SIMaided multiuser multiple-input single-output(MISO) downlink systems under statistical CSI. We formulate the achievable sum rate maximization problem considering practical discrete phase constraints and derive a closed-form expression for the average achievable rate under statistical CSI. To tackle the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, we decouple the problem by using the weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) algorithm and alternating optimization (AO). Subsequently, we utilize the Lagrangian multiplier method and alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) to obtain closed-form iterative solutions. Our simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm reduces computational complexity by a factor of 50 compared to semi-definite relaxation (SDR) methods, while maintaining over 85 % of the continuous phase shift performance with only 1-bit quantization, highlighting its feasibility for low-cost hardware systems.

title: Joint Channel Estimation and Equalization for MU-MIMO-OFDM Uplink Based on Spatial-Temporal-Frequency GNN.
abstract: Multi-user multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MU-MIMO-OFDM) is a key technology for modern wireless communications, supporting high data rates and multi-user access. However, conventional approaches that perform channel estimation and equalization separately often suffer from error propagation, where inaccuracies in channel estimates adversely affect the subsequent multiuser detection and equalization process, leading to degraded overall performance. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a deep learning-based framework for joint channel estimation and equalization in MU-MIMO-OFDM uplink systems using a spatial-temporal-frequency graph neural network (STF-GNN). The proposed network architecture is designed to effectively exploit the inherent correlations in the spatial, temporal, and frequency domains, enabling more accurate and robust signal recovery. Experiment results demonstrate that the proposed joint method achieves a gain of 2-4 dB, which translates to a significant reduction in both the mean square error (MSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) of the recovered constellation symbols compared to traditional separated approaches.

title: On the Stabilizability and Scheduling of Wireless Control Network Design with RSMA.
abstract: Wireless control networks (WCNs) have been regarded as the key enablers of industrial Internet of Things (IoT) applications to provide intelligent and automatic services. This paper studies a multi-subsystem WCN in which a remote base station (BS) acquires plant states and delivers processed observations to the corresponding controllers over shared downlink channels. Given limited transmit power budgets and heterogeneous control requirements, we formulate a control scheduling and beamforming design problem based on rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) with finite blocklength (FBL). In particular, the system-level information, e.g., overall mission duration, is mapped into common messages that each subsystem needs to decode, while the corresponding observations are encoded as private data streams. The impact of communication performance on control stabilizability is analyzed. Subsequently, a computationally efficient iterative algorithm is proposed to address the resultant non-convex optimization problem. Extensive simulations have been conducted to validate the effectiveness of our proposed method and reveal the non-trivial tradeoff between wireless control stabilizability and scheduling.

title: TRILLM: Triple-Based Semantic Communication with LLMS for Robust IIoT Communication.
abstract: This paper presents a triple-based large language model (LLM)-to-LLM (TRILLM) semantic communication framework for handling semantically impaired industrial internet of things (IIoT) text. We consider a system with N edge devices where each device uses a lightweight LLM to compress event-driven messages into triple representations before transmission to a central hub equipped with an LLMbased semantic decoder. To better evaluate reconstruction quality under semantic impairments, we introduce a semantic equivalence metric that combines cosine similarity with grammar fluency. We further analyze the rate and latency characteristics of the proposed framework. Simulation results show that TRILLM achieves up to 67% higher semantic equivalence than baseline knowledge graph (KG)-based schemes, demonstrating improved robustness in impaired IIoT text communication. Additionally, TRILLM offers adaptability and contextual reasoning advantages over KG approaches

title: Reinforcement Learning Based Multiple UE Link Selection in 5G mm-wave Channels.
abstract: The use of High-frequency bands such as the millimeter-wave (mm-wave) are one of the key technologies for enabling high-speed wireless communication in future mobile networks. However, high-frequency bands are difficult to handle due to their high straightness and severe attenuation caused by blockage from obstacles, making communication stability a significant challenge. The instability of the high-frequency band becomes particularly prominent in wireless access links, as blockage by the user's own body occurs frequently. We have therefore been investigating multiple user equipment (UE) cooperation to stabilize the mm-wave access link among multiple mm-wave-capable UEs owned by a single user. Stable communication is achieved through selection diversity across different access links of UEs in the close vicinity of the user. In this paper, we propose a deep-Q-learning (DQL)-based proactive UE link selection method and perform experimental evaluation using commercial smartphones in an indoor 5 G area. Our proposal predicts the connection UE link to be used one second in advance, realizing proactive control that simultaneously stabilizes throughput and reduces power consumption. The results of experiments demonstrate that the proposed method can improve the$\mathbf{1 0} \boldsymbol{\%}$-ile throughput cumulative distribution function (CDF) by about$\mathbf{1 0} \boldsymbol{\%}$with$\mathbf{1 5} \boldsymbol{\%}$lower power consumption compared to the conventional reference signal received power (RSRP) based switching method.

title: Detecting Convolutional Codes via a Markovian Statistic.
abstract: Identifying the unknown channel code corresponding to the given intercepted data is an important problem in military surveillance and in wireless communication. In this paper, we focus on the situation when the given data corresponds to either of the two potential convolutional codes and the goal is to detect the correct code. While a variety of code detection algorithms are available in the literature, the key contribution of our work lies in the novel solution and the corresponding analysis. We decode the received data via Viterbi algorithm using either of the code and consider the corresponding sequence of Viterbi metric for code detection. We identify that the sequence of Viterbi metric follows a Markov chain (MC) and formulate the code detection problem as a hypothesis testing between two MCs. We provide a method to find the state-transition matrices for the two MCs and study the analytical asymptotic performance via the associated error exponent. We validate the performance of our method via a variety of simulations and also compare our performance with the method available in the literature.

title: Neural Network Approach for Real-Time Antenna Pattern Generation and Eirp Prediction.
abstract: In massive multiple-input, multiple-output (mMIMO) beamforming, antenna gain is increased in certain directions to adapt to instantaneous user distributions. Standardized methods, such as IEC62232 [1] use an actual maximum approach to assess human exposure to radio frequency (RF) electromagnetic fields (EMF). These methods monitor the actual EIRP (Effective Isotropic Radiated Power) and control it. During operation, this control ensures that the EIRP does not exceed the thresholds required for RF EMF exposure compliance within the related averaging time. This can be implemented either over the total cell or on cell segments. To meet these requirements, the EIRP of the gNB needs to be calculated dynamically, independently of the mMIMO beamforming algorithm. However, no current system provides highly accurate EIRP control for weight vectors computed dynamically. Additionally, in open radio access network (ORAN) standards, radio units may be owned by different vendors. Direct computation of the EIRP would require the exchange of proprietary information between the radio unit (O-RU) and the distributed unit (O-DU). We propose an artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) framework for accurate computation of EIRP dynamically, without requiring any exchange of proprietary information between O-RU and O-DU vendors. This is a crucial requirement for future O-RAN products. We demonstrate that, using convolutional deep neural networks, the EIRP can be determined with high accuracy, achieving a tolerance of 0.1 dB for beam gain values within 5 dB from the peak and 1 dB for beam gains within 30 dB from the peak in our evaluation test cases.

title: Edge-Optimized ExmobileViT: A Lightweight Vision Transformer for Multi-Class Alzheimer's MRI Classification.
abstract: Early identification of Alzheimer's disease (AD) is critical for enabling timely clinical intervention and improving long-term patient outcomes. Although Vision Transformers (ViTs) have demonstrated exceptional representational capacity for medical imaging tasks, their substantial computational requirements limit deployment on resource-constrained platforms such as edge-enabled Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) systems. This work introduces ExMobileViT, a lightweight and hardwareefficient ViT enhanced with Ghost modules, explicitly designed for multi-class AD classification from structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The model emphasizes reduced latency and minimal memory footprint, providing an operational advantage for portable and real-time neurodiagnostic inference. Experimental evaluation against standard ViT and MobileViT baselines demonstrates that ExMobileViT achieves 95% accuracy and a macro F1 score of 0.96, while operating with approximately 1.11 million parameters and 0.36 GFLOPs. These results verify that ExMobileViT sustains strong diagnostic performance with substantially lower computational cost. Although interpretability and clinician validation remain future objectives, the findings demonstrate the potential suitability of ExMobileViT for efficient and scalable transformer-based intelligence in resourceconstrained IoMT healthcare environments.

title: Pilot Assignment for Distributed Massive MIMO Based on Channel Estimation Error Minimization.
abstract: Pilot contamination remains a major bottleneck in realizing the full potential of distributed massive MIMO systems. We propose two dynamic and scalable pilot assignment schemes designed for practical deployment in such networks. First, we present a low-complexity centralized scheme that sequentially assigns pilots to user equipments (UEs) to minimize the global channel estimation errors across serving access points (APs). This improves the channel estimation quality and reduces interference among UEs, enhancing the spectral efficiency. Second, we develop a fully distributed scheme that uses a priority-based pilot selection approach. In this scheme, each selected AP minimizes the channel estimation error using only local information and offers candidate pilots to the UEs. Every UE then selects a suitable pilot based on its AP priority. This approach ensures consistency and minimizes interference while significantly reducing pilot contamination. The method requires no global coordination, maintains low signaling overhead, and adapts dynamically to the UE deployment. Numerical simulations demonstrate the superiority of the proposed schemes in terms of network throughput when compared to the existing state-of-the-art schemes.

title: Propagation Channel Modeling for LEO Satellite Missions Using Ray-Tracing Simulations.
abstract: This work presents a high-resolution, ray-tracing-based channel modeling for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite-to-ground links in a suburban environment at X-band. Using simulations conducted in Wireless InSite, we develop a parametric channel model that characterizes both large- and small-scale fading effects across different satellite elevation angles. Large-scale fading incorporates attenuation due to terrain-induced shadowing and dynamic environmental factors such as weather conditions, and is compared with 3GPP NTN channel model. Additionally, we quantify link degradation resulting from ground station (GS) antenna misalignment, considering both fixed single-element and electronically steerable phased-array antennas. Small-scale fading is modeled by fitting a shadowed and non-shadowed Rician distribution to the fading statistics at various satellite elevations. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to propose a comprehensive elevation-aware channel model for satellite-to-ground propagation at X-band, integrating ray-traced environmental dynamics, elevation-dependent fading, and phased-array beam misalignment effects.

title: A High-Precision Assisted Timing Support Mechanism for Edge Access Points.
abstract: This paper presents a standards-compliant Edge Access Point (EAP) architecture that delivers precise synchronization for emerging time-sensitive wireless applications in Industrial IoT, autonomous systems, and$\mathbf{5 G}$networks. To overcome the sub-microsecond accuracy limitations of existing wireless protocols, the proposed EAP is the first architecture that integrates the ITU-T Assisted Partial Timing Support (APTS) model with two innovations: (i) hardware-assisted Precision Time Protocol (PTP) time-stamping via an extended Timing Synchronization Function (TSF) counter, and (ii) wireless emulation of Synchronous Ethernet (SyncE). The design supports Telecom Grandmaster clock requirements through dual timing references, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) input and a PTP stream, ensuring Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) traceability within$\pm \mathbf{1 0 0 ~ n s}$. Simulation results demonstrate dynamic performance well within$\mathbf{\pm 1 0 0 ~ n s}$, with Oven-Controlled Crystal Oscillator (OCXO)-based holdover stability better than$\mathbf{1 0 0 ~ n s}$for up to four hours. Furthermore, client-side evaluations incorporating 10 ns transmit time-stamping error highlight substantial phase error reduction, while the wireless-recovered SyncE clock eliminates the need for high-stability (better than 1 ppm) local oscillators. These results establish the proposed EAP as a practical and robust solution for high-precision synchronization in next-generation wireless networks.

title: Channel Estimation for Pinching Antennas Systems using Deep Learning.
abstract: Pinching antennas (PAs) are novel type of antenna that leverage dielectric waveguides and electromagnetic coupling to mitigate large-scale path loss. Channel estimation in PA systems is highly challenging, as it represents an ill-posed problem due to the underdetermined nature of the channel characteristics. This creates a strong need for efficient estimation techniques. In this work, a deep learning framework is proposed that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with artificial neural networks (ANNs) to estimate channel coefficients on a per-antenna basis, thereby providing greater flexibility and adaptability to varying numbers of PAs in practical deployment scenarios. While the proposed CNN-ANN method delivers efficient performance compared to the conventional approach, it also has low computational complexity.

title: An Elastic Clustering Framework for Large-Scale WSNs Maximizing Network Lifetime.
abstract: Large-scale Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are applied in multiple domains, notably Precision Agriculture, Intelligent Traffic Management and Smart Hospital. A key task for these applications, long-term environment monitoring, relies on periodic data collection via network clustering. In applications like precision agriculture, large networks requires frequent topology updates to avoid hotspot issues at Cluster Heads (CHs), balance energy consumption, and meet QoS demands. Centralized topology maintenance at the Base Station ensures global energy efficiency but incurs costly networkwide control overhead in larger deployments. This undermines existing LEACH-derived and even recent protocols using treebased approaches, in terms of scalability. We propose PECEE, a framework combining centralized CH selection with local routing coordination, enabling elastic clustering for raw data collection. Simulations show that PECEE extends network lifetime from$\mathbf{5 0 \%}$to$\mathbf{9 0 \%}$compared to some notable solutions including GSTEB [11] in raw data collection simulations, and up to 200 % when data aggregation is used.

title: MARBLE-Net: Learning to Localize in Multipath Environment with Adaptive Rainbow Beams.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems demand precise and efficient target localization, a task challenged by rich multipath propagation in complex wireless environments. This paper introduces MARBLE-Net (Multipath-Aware Rainbow Beam Learning Network), a deep learning framework that jointly optimizes the analog beamforming parameters of a frequency-dependent rainbow beam and a neural localization network for high-accuracy position estimation. By treating the phase-shifter (PS) and true-time-delay (TTD) parameters as learnable weights, the system adaptively refines its sensing beam to exploit environment-specific multipath characteristics. A structured multi-stage training strategy is proposed to ensure stable convergence and effective end-to-end optimization. Simulation results show that MARBLE-Net outperforms both a fixed-beam deep learning baseline (RaiNet) and a traditional k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) method, reducing localization error by more than 50\% in a multipath-rich scene. Moreover, the results reveal a nuanced interaction with multipath propagation: while confined uni-directional multipath degrades accuracy, structured and directional multipath can be effectively exploited to achieve performance surpassing even line-of-sight (LoS) conditions.

title: CP-Aided AFDM Channel Estimation for High-Mobility Scenarios.
abstract: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) is a promising multicarrier waveform for high-mobility scenarios due to its robustness against doubly-dispersive channels. However, accurate channel estimation remains challenging because delay and Doppler shifts are coupled in the discrete affine Fourier transform (DAFT) domain. In this paper, unlike conventional AFDM channel estimation schemes that rely on a relatively large chirp parameter to maintain path separability in doubly-dispersive channels, we develop a CP-based channel estimation scheme without this requirement. This makes the proposed method more suitable for channels with large delay spreads, where conventional designs would otherwise suffer from high pilot overhead. Specifically, the cross-correlation between the cyclic prefix (CP) and the corresponding symbol tail is computed over multiple symbols and averaged to estimate the Doppler shifts. The path delays are then identified using pilots in the DAFT domain, based on which an equivalent channel matrix is constructed for DAFT-domain equalization. Crucially, we show that under random signaling, the phase of the CP cross-correlation depends only on the Doppler shifts and is invariant to multipath interference. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a Doppler normalized mean square error (NMSE) of$10^{-3}$at an SNR of 17 dB. Moreover, the proposed CP-AFDM scheme demonstrates superior BER performance over conventional multicarrier waveforms.

title: Physical-Informed Radio Map Estimation: An Environment-Aware Decomposition Approach.
abstract: High-resolution Radio Map Estimation (RME) is a key enabling technology for environment-aware communications. Existing deep learning approaches often treat the radio map monolithically, ignoring its intrinsic physical structure. In practice, radio maps exhibit a fundamental structural dichotomy: Predictable, smooth Line-of-Sight (LoS) regions and complex, stochastic Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) regions governed by multipath phenomena. In this paper, a physics-informed hybrid framework is proposed that decomposes the RME task according to this dichotomy. The framework employs a deterministic regression model to estimate the LoS component and a conditional generative model to estimate the NLoS component. For NLoS estimation, conditional flow matching is leveraged as an efficient and simulation-free alternative to computationally intensive diffusion models. Our framework is validated on a ray-tracing-based dataset. Experiments demonstrate that our hybrid approach significantly outperforms conventional schemes, validating our hypothesis that the decomposition of the problem based on its underlying physics leads to a more accurate and efficient model.

title: Passive Synthetic Aperture Equivalent Model and Localization for Spaceborne Squint Scenario.
abstract: In wireless emitter monitoring scenarios, space-borne passive localization technology has garnered significant attention due to its advantages such as wide-area coverage and all-weather operation. Conventional localization methods, such as Direction of Arrival (DOA) and Frequency Difference of Arrival (FDOA), rely on instantaneous measurements and process signals non-coherently over time. Consequently, their accuracy degrades significantly under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. In recent years, passive synthetic aperture (PSA) techniques have been applied to emitter localization, enhancing localization precision through coherent integration of the Doppler phase to achieve high processing gain. An accurate PSA method requires precise modeling of the Doppler history. However, existing models predominantly assume linear platform motion, which introduces a fundamental model mismatch by neglecting orbital and Earth curvature effects. This omission leads to inaccuracies in Doppler history reconstruction and ultimately limits their applicability in practical spaceborne missions. To address these limitations, this study first establishes an equivalent squint model for spaceborne passive localization scenarios, then provides rigorous definitions of the equivalent parameters, and finally proposes a PSA localization method tailored for spaceborne squint conditions, thus extending the applicability of the spaceborne PSA method to squint scenarios. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an order-of-magnitude improvement in localization accuracy over conventional FDOA and DOA methods under low-SNR conditions, while maintaining high-precision localization capability despite large squint angles. The practical efficacy of the approach is further confirmed via a satellite experiment.

title: Link Adaptation for ISAC Systems over Imperfect Vehicle-to-Infrastructure Channels.
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) technology holds significant promise for future vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) networks by enabling joint resource utilization. However, imperfect wireless channels with mixed line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) components pose challenges to reliable adaptive modulation (AM). Accordingly, this paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-driven link adaptation strategy for ISAC systems in such dynamic V2I environments. Unlike conventional pilot-dependent methods, our approach leverages historical radar echo signals to predict modulation modes, eliminating pilot overhead, and enhancing spectral efficiency. A convolutional soft actor-critic dueling network (Conv-SAC-D-Net) is designed to extract spatiotemporal features from multi-dimensional echo matrices, enabling accurate modulation selection while bypassing channel estimation and matched filtering. The framework dynamically balances capacity maximization and bit error rate (BER) constraints through a dual-policy mechanism, prioritizing reliability near mode-switching thresholds. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly enhances both channel reliability and spectral efficiency compared to traditional pilot-based AM schemes.

title: RLCVP: Collaborative Vehicular Perception Against Data Fabrication Attacks.
abstract: Collaborative vehicular perception enables connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) to share sensing data such as light detection and ranging (LiDAR) point clouds for higher perception accuracy and speed, which has performance degradation against data fabrication attacks that send faked sensing data with random probability. In this paper, a spatial consistency check is proposed to verify received feature maps, which builds a test statistic based on the number of conflict object locations in point clouds to detect faked sensing data. The reinforcement learning-based collaborative vehicular perception scheme is further proposed to enhance accuracy and speed, which chooses collaborative CAVs based on the geometry inconsistency of object locations, the data quality, the channel gains and the CAV reputations. Simulation results in LiDAR-based object detection show performance gains over benchmarks in terms of perception accuracy and speed against data fabrication attacks that manipulate up to$\mathbf{1 0}$regions in point clouds.

title: A Distributed Offloading Strategy Considering Information Freshness in Drone Swarms.
abstract: In future 6G networks, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) can provide efficient communication and computing services. But due to limited computing and battery resources, UAVs often need to offload tasks to edge base stations or Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. To make full use of drone networks, multihop communication can be used for computation offloading. In this process, User Equipment (UE) first offloads computation tasks to a local UAV. This UAV processes part of the task and offloads the rest to a neighboring UAV. This continues until the task is done. However, during multi-hop offloading, UAVs may experience state information lag because of unstable communication links. This paper proposes a distributed computation offloading method that combines a predictor with multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). The predictor models state updates and predictions, and Lyapunov stability theory ensures its stability. To handle uncertainties in multi-hop UAV offloading, the Multiagent Bidirectionally-Coordinated Nets (BiCNet) is used to optimize task processing and resource management. Simulation results show that this method effectively reduces latency and energy consumption in multi-hop UAV computation offloading.

title: Symbol-Synchronous Communication for Ultra-Low-Power Multi-Hop Ambient IoT Networks.
abstract: Ambient Internet of Things (A-IoT) devices, as a critical enabler of future green IoT networks, have attracted broad interest from both industry and academia due to their ability to operate without batteries and with low maintenance costs. To accommodate their dynamic and constrained energy budget, an ultra-low-power connectivity protocol is required. Due to the severely limited transmit power of A-IoT devices, multi-hop connectivity is an interesting paradigm to extend their range. However, commonly used protocols for multi-hop communication may not be suitable for A-IoT due to excessive overhead related to channel access procedures, coordinated routing, and tight time synchronization requirements. This paper presents a novel network connectivity protocol based on symbolsynchronous transmissions, which allows battery-less relay nodes to participate in the forwarding process in an ad-hoc manner, without the need for synchronization or coordination. This allows them to adapt their duty cycle to the available harvested energy. Simulation results show that the proposed protocol can ensure high reliability in data packet delivery while significantly reducing the energy consumption of each relay node. We also investigate the relationship between wake-up probability and network density. For example, a 400 -node network in a 625 m2area can achieve a packet error rate below 1% with an average awake time of 6% per node, achieving an energy consumption reduction of 88% compared to the baseline approach.

title: Queue-Aware RL Scheduling with Stability Bounds in Large-Scale Cellular Networks.
abstract: This paper investigates adaptive transmission scheduling in large-scale cellular networks under dynamic traffic and interference conditions. Using stochastic geometry to capture spatial interference and incorporating queue dynamics at each base station, we aim to minimize long-term transmission cost subject to a delay constraint, via a Lagrangian relaxation. The problem is formulated as a constrained Markov decision process and solved via lightweight online reinforcement learning algorithms that adapts decisions to traffic and channel conditions. In parallel, we derive a stability bound from baseline policies through meta-distribution analysis, which provides benchmarks for dynamic scheduling policies. Numerical results show that the RL-based policies hold the same stability region as the baseline, while reducing the long-term Lagrangian cost by 26-30% under moderate to heavy loads, and up to 42% under light loads.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Metamaterial Backscatter for Symbiotic Sensing and Communication.
abstract: The future 6 G network aims to integrate batteryfree Internet of Things (IoT) devices to acquire massive environmental data. However, current battery-free IoT devices are often limited to simple identification tasks and lack diverse sensing capabilities. Fortunately, metamaterial sensing tags can reflect cellular signals to facilitate high-sensitivity environmental sensing while simultaneously serving as a reflection surface to enhance user communication. However, this dual functionality creates an inherent trade-off, as the cellular signals must carry original data while being modulated by the tag for sensing, leading to resource competition. This paper proposes a symbiotic meta-backscatter system to explicitly manage this conflict. We first derive a lower bound for communication capacity and an upper bound for sensing mutual information as unified performance metrics. Based on these metrics, we formulate a multi-objective optimization problem (MOOP) to jointly optimize the metamaterial tag's physical design and the base station's beamforming matrix. Simulation results demonstrate that our framework offers flexible trade-off solutions between sensing accuracy and communication quality.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: RAS: Reconfiguration-Aware Adaptive Video Streaming Over Satellite Networks.
abstract: Live streaming has experienced rapid growth in recent years. In the meanwhile, commercial companies such as SpaceX and Amazon are providing low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellite network services to millions of global users. As a result, an increasing number of users are using LEO satellite networks (LSNs) to watch live streaming videos on their devices. The bandwidth however owns a low upper limit and exhibits significant fluctuations due to satellite handovers and atmospheric conditions compared to terrestrial networks. This poses a challenge for scenarios that rely on LSNs for live streaming as the existing adaptive video streaming system cannot adapt to such highly dynamic network conditions which leads to low link utilization and a high frequency of video bitrate switches. To address these challenges, we propose RAS (Reconfiguration-aware Adaptive video streaming over Satellite networks), including a novel adaptive bitrate (ABR) algorithm designed specifically for LSNs and a reconfiguration predictor. RAS leverages the inherent nature of satellite links caused by reconfiguration events, which divide the time domain into a sequence of independent subintervals. Our evaluation demonstrates that RAS significantly reduces bitrate instability and improves quality of experience (QoE) in real world. Compared with state-of-the-art ABR algorithms, RAS improves mean QoE score by more than 60%, while reducing switching rate by over 65%.

title: Modeling and Parameter Estimation of Air-to-Ground Channels Using a Mixture of Skew Normal Distributions.
abstract: With the rapid development of Air-To-Ground (A2G) communications, the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) has become an important enabling technology of future wireless communication systems. In complex urban environments, wireless links alternates between two typical contrary conditions, i.e., Line-of-Sight (LoS) and Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS), due to channel dynamics caused by the UAVs' high mobility. To better understand the characteristics of A2G channels, we study its statistical modeling with samples of path loss collected through ray-trace-based simulation in 3D city maps. After in-depth empirical study, we use mixed skew normal mixture distribution as the fitting model and propose a conditional Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm to estimate the model parameters. Simulation results show that the proposed model effectively fits the skewness and heterogeneity of the path loss, which significantly contributes to design and performance evaluation of UAV communication systems, especially in urban regions.

title: ViChan: A Dataset Generation Framework for Vision-aided Channel Estimation with Deep Learning.
abstract: Channel estimation is imperative for system design in wireless communications and is commonly computationally intensive with non-negligible overhead. Vision information is potentially a helpful assist for channel estimation since physical environment significantly affects radio propagation. Moreover, deep learning models for computer vision support better scene understanding and thus is a proper candidate technique for vision-aided channel estimation while being well trained with sufficient data. With such motivations, in this paper, we proposed ViChan, a novel and low-cost framework for generating paired image-channel dataset, which integrates two off-the-shelf tools for wireless channel simulation and environment image capture, respectively. Though the two modules are independent with each other, they operates in parallel and no interaction needs to be designed with ViChan. With such a cost-effective approach, the ground-truth channel information can be associated with the real-world environment images via appropriately designed indexing. Such a solid dataset of paired image-channel samples promisingly enables vision-aided channel estimation through design and training of deep learning models, boosting awareness, perceptiveness and intelligence of wireless networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: MmWave Beam Prediction with Data Augmentation.
abstract: Deep learning has achieved outstanding performance in millimeter-wave (mmWave) beam prediction, whereas acquiring the optimal beam labels for model training imposes excessive overhead. To address this issue, this paper proposes to adopt data augmentation to efficiently train the mmWave beam prediction models with limited data. Specifically, two different data augmentation, namely input augmentation and label augmentation, are investigated. For input augmentation, cyclic shifting, flipping, and noise injection are used to extend the data features. For label augmentation, to fully leverage the guidance of sub-optimal beams, a power function of normalized beam received amplitude is used to redefine the label, and an adaptive exponent scheduler is employed to facilitate the model optimization. Simulation results show that our proposed approach significantly outperforms the conventional supervised learning methods in terms of normalized beamforming gain and model convergence rate, especially with extremely limited data.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Divergence Meets Dispersion: Efficient Wideband Beam Training for XL-MIMO.
abstract: Wideband extremely large-scale MIMO (XLMIMO) is a key enabler for 6 G networks, providing high spatial resolution and strong beamforming gains at millimeter-wave frequencies. However, efficient beam training under wideband and near-field (NF) conditions remains challenging due to hardware constraints and complex propagation characteristics. To address this, we propose a diverging-and-dispersion effect-based wideband beam training scheme that mitigates the deviation sensitivity of conventional focusing beams. The diverging effect broadens spatial coverage, while the dispersion effect introduces frequency-dependent beam splitting, jointly enabling efficient coarse beam search with fewer subcarriers and improved spectral efficiency. Moreover, the diverging codeword relies solely on phase modulation with constant amplitude, reducing hardware complexity. We further design an efficient dual-function system architecture, allowing simultaneous beam training and communication over the entire antenna array. Building on it, a lowoverhead wideband NF beam training algorithm is developed, achieving performance comparable to optimal benchmarks while significantly reducing resource usage. Simulation results verify the proposed method's robustness and efficiency, making it a practical solution for next-generation 6G XL-MIMO systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Large Language Models as Bidding Agents in Repeated HetNet Auction.
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of large language models (LLMs) as reasoning agents in repeated spectrum auctions within heterogeneous networks (HetNets). While auction-based mechanisms have been widely employed for efficient resource allocation, most prior works assume one-shot auctions, static bidder behavior, and idealized conditions. In contrast to traditional formulations where base station (BS) association and power allocation are centrally optimized, we propose a distributed auction-based framework in which each BS independently conducts its own multi-channel auction, and user equipments (UEs) strategically decide both their association and bid values. Within this setting, UEs operate under budget constraints and repeated interactions, transforming resource allocation into a long-term economic decision rather than a oneshot optimization problem. The proposed framework enables the evaluation of diverse bidding behaviors-from classical myopic and greedy policies to LLM-based agents capable of reasoning over historical outcomes, anticipating competition, and adapting their bidding strategy across episodes. Simulation results reveal that the LLM-empowered UE consistently achieves higher channel access frequency and improved budget efficiency compared to benchmarks. These findings highlight the potential of reasoningenabled agents in future decentralized wireless networks markets and pave the way for lightweight, edge-deployable LLMs to support intelligent resource allocation in next-generation HetNets.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-LEO Satellite Transmission with Terrestrial Coexistence: A Coverage-Enhanced and Interference-Mitigated Framework.
abstract: The integration of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites with terrestrial base stations (TBSs) is envisioned as a cornerstone of future wireless networks. However, coexistence of dense terrestrial deployments with large-scale LEO constellations introduces a fundamental challenge: maximizing LEO throughput while strictly protecting terrestrial users from harmful interference. In this work, we propose a coverage-enhanced and interference-mitigated power allocation (CIPA) framework that adaptively controls the transmit power of multi-beam LEO satellites under interference constraints at TBS-served users. By jointly applying the Lagrangian dual and quadratic transforms, the originally non-convex problem is reformulated into tractable subproblems with closed-form auxiliary updates and convex power allocation, ensuring provable equivalence and efficient convergence. Extensive simulations on both synthetic deployments and real automatic identification system (AIS) maritime datasets demonstrate that CIPA not only achieves substantial throughput gains but also enhances user coverage by dynamically balancing load between LEO and TBS layers. Compared with existing benchmarks, CIPA yields at least 28.9% throughput improvement while remaining close to brute-force performance at a fraction of the complexity. These results highlight CIPA as a practical and near-optimal resource management solution for integrated terrestrial-satellite networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Toward an Intrusion Detection System for a Virtualization Framework in Edge Computing.
abstract: Edge computing pushes computation closer to data sources, but it also expands the attack surface on resource-constrained devices. This work explores the deployment of the Lightweight Deep Anomaly Detection for Network Traffic (LDPI) integrated as an isolated service within a virtualization framework that provides security by separation. LDPI, adopting a Deep Learning approach, achieved strong training performance, reaching AUC 0.999 (5-fold mean) across the evaluated packet-window settings (n, l), with high F1 at conservative operating points. We deploy LDPI on a laptop-class edge node and evaluate its overhead and performance in two scenarios: (i) comparing it with representative signature-based IDSes (Suricata and Snort) deployed on the same framework under identical workloads, and (ii) while detecting network flooding attacks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Lightweight Dual-Level Fusion Network for MIMO Automatic Modulation Recognition.
abstract: Low-altitude wireless networks (LAWN) operate in untrusted open environments, making them vulnerable to malicious attacks. However, automatic modulation recognition (AMR) can identify the modulation schemes of unknown signals, thereby detecting illegal interference and safeguarding the security of wireless communication environments. Although deep learning (DL) has significantly improved AMR performance, research on its application in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems remains limited, and existing fusion strategies are confined to single fusion approaches. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a lightweight dual-level fusion network (LDLFN) architecture. The framework innovatively incorporates a depthwise separable convolution module to process signals from each receiving antenna in parallel, generating antenna-level feature representations and preliminary classification decisions. Subsequently, joint feature fusion and preliminary decision fusion are performed across antennas. Finally, the feature fusion results are combined with the preliminary decisions through a secondary fusion step to output a highly robust modulation classification outcome. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method reduces computational cost by 60% and parameters by 25% compared to Triple-Skip Residual Neural Network (TRNN), while achieving an average accuracy improvement of 2.58%.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Analysis of Localization and CoMP Transmission Performance in Integrated Sensing and Communication Networks.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) technology enables high-resolution sensing and high data rate communication through shared hardware, becoming a key enabler for future networks. However, this integration disrupts traditional system architecture, requiring coordination of sensing and communication under resource constraints and a unified framework to characterize their coupling. In this work, we propose a stochastic geometry-based modeling and performance evaluation framework for ISAC networks, where users and roadside units (RSUs) are modeled as a Matérn cluster process. Users send data to intra-cluster RSUs, which estimate and return the Cramér-Rao lower bound for localization performance evaluation. Upon successful localization, RSUs transmit data via coordinated multipoint, and the conditional communication coverage probability is evaluated. The overall performance is then derived using conditional probability and validated through simulations and numerical analysis.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Beamforming and Antenna Position Optimization for Active ND-RIS-Assisted DFRC Systems with Movable Antenna Arrays.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has emerged as a key enabling technology for future 6 G networks by allowing radar sensing and wireless communication to coexist within a unified framework. In this paper, we investigate an active non-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface (ND-RIS)-assisted dual-functional radar-communication (DFRC) system aided by a movable antenna (MA) array at the base station (BS). By jointly exploiting the electromagnetic flexibility of active ND-RIS and the spatial adaptability introduced by MA positioning, the proposed architecture enables enhanced control over both signal propagation and spatial beamforming. We formulate a joint optimization problem to maximize the minimum radar beampattern gain subject to user signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) requirements, BS transmit power constraints, active RIS amplification limits, and physical antenna separation constraints. The resulting problem is highly non-convex due to the coupled design variables and hardware-induced constraints. To address this challenge, an alternating optimization framework is developed, where the transmit covariance matrix, active ND-RIS reflection matrix, and MA positions are optimized iteratively using semidefinite relaxation, quadratically constrained quadratic programming, and successive convex approximation techniques. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed MA-assisted active ND-RIS framework significantly outperforms conventional passive RIS and fixed-position antenna baselines in terms of radar beam-pattern sharpness, communication robustness, and sensing-communication trade-offs, highlighting its potential for next-generation ISAC systems.

title: Diffusion Model - Assisted Task-Oriented Semantic Communication with DRL-Based Resource Optimization.
abstract: This paper presents a task-oriented semantic communication network (TOSCN) that integrates the Task-Oriented Channel Denoiser (TOCD), a diffusion-model-based module designed to enhance the semantic robustness of transmitted features. By adaptively adjusting the number of denoising steps, TOCD balances the latency-accuracy trade-off, improving task performance under poor channel conditions while minimizing redundant computation in favorable environments. We formulate a joint optimization problem of bandwidth, transmit power, and denoising time to maximize long-term transmission efficiency and model it as a Markov decision process (MDP). A deep reinforcement learning (DRL)–based resource allocation scheme is then developed to learn adaptive policies that allocate resources according to real-time channel states, buffer conditions, and accuracy requirements. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms both DRL baselines and greedy allocation methods across multiple accuracy constraints. The results confirm that combining diffusion-based denoising with DRL-driven optimization achieves robust, accuracy-aware, and resource-efficient task-oriented communication, offering a promising direction for next-generation intelligent wireless networks.

title: Deep Learning-Based Zak-OTFS Receiver with Embedded and Interleaved Pilots.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based receiver architecture for joint input-output (I/O) relation estimation and signal detection in Zak transform-based orthogonal time frequency space (Zak-OTFS) systems. Embedded and interleaved pilot frames are considered, where pilot and data symbols coexist in a given frame and interfere with each other. A fully-connected deep neural network (DNN) is trained to jointly learn the effective delay-Doppler (DD) channel and optimize detection performance as a single task. The proposed deep learning approach is found to effectively handle inter-symbol interference and achieve better bit error rate performance compared to conventional methods that perform the channel estimation and signal detection tasks separately. Even with reduced guard region overhead in embedded pilot frames (high throughput and increased interference), the proposed receiver is found to deliver robust performance, while traditional techniques perform poorly. Further, the deep learning-based receiver is shown to work effectively with interleaved pilot frames, which offer the benefits of increased throughput (due to no guard region between pilot and data) and reduced peak-to-average power ratio.

title: An Entropy-Driven Gradient Variance Attack on Automatic Modulation Classification.
abstract: Deep learning-based automatic modulation classification (AMC) systems have been widely studied, recent studies demonstrate their vulnerability to adversarial attacks. However, in practical wireless communication scenarios, such attacks often fail due to channel-induced perturbation distortion and poor transferability in multi-user heterogeneous scenarios. To overcome these limitations, we propose an Entropy-Driven Variance Gradient Sign Method (EVGSM) for effective adversarial attacks. Our approach integrates a diversity loss term with the cross-entropy loss to form an Entropy-Diversity Balanced Loss (EDBL), preventing adversarial samples from converging to the trivial solutions under channel fading. Simultaneously, a Momentum-based Gradient Variance Tuning (MGVT) mechanism enhances gradient exploration diversity, mitigating fading effects and improving transferability across diverse scenarios. Empirical evidence demonstrates that EVGSM outperforms state-of-the-art methods in wireless environments.

title: Qudit Selection for Amplitude Damping Quantum Channel.
abstract: Amplitude-damping (AD) noise, which models energy relaxation and spontaneous decay, is a dominant source of decoherence in quantum systems such as atoms, ions, photonics, and superconducting qubits. While the qubit (two-level) AD channel has been extensively analyzed, its generalization to higherdimensional systems (qudits) remains less explored despite their practical relevance. This paper develops a systematic framework to evaluate and compare the performance of qubits and qudits under amplitude-damping noise. Closed-form expressions are derived for several fidelity measures, including computational basis, equal superposition, and Haar-average fidelities. We then numerically estimate the single-letter coherent information$Q_{1}$as a lower bound on the quantum capacity. A normalized performance score combining fidelity and capacity is proposed to identify optimal qudit dimensions across different damping probabilities. Simulation results reveal that higher-dimensional systems can outperform qubits in low-noise regimes, while qubits remain more robust under strong damping. The resulting “recommendation map” offers practical guidance for the experimental selection of qudit dimension in amplitude-damping environments.

title: Networked ISAC for 3D Air-Corridor: Joint UAV Trajectory and Beamforming Design.
abstract: This paper investigates air-corridor-constrained UAV trajectory planning and beamforming optimization for networked integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) with distributed ground base stations (GBSs). A single UAV flies within a predefined air-corridor while receiving cooperative downlink communication from multiple distributed GBSs, which simultaneously conduct sensing over a designated monitoring airspace. A joint optimization problem is formulated to maximize the long-term average communication rate of the UAV subject to power limitations, point-wise sensing energy requirements, UAV kinematic constraints, and strict air-corridor compliance. To address the strong coupling and non-convexity between the UAV trajectory and the ISAC beamforming design, we develop a constrained proximal policy optimization (PPO) framework. For a fixed trajectory, cooperative communication and sensing beamforming are optimized via semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and fractional programming (FP). The UAV trajectory optimization is structured as a nested process. A PPO-based reinforcement learning outer loop for policy guidance is tightly integrated with an inner loop of beamforming, which integrates the air-corridor constraints into the decision process. Numerical results verify that the proposed air-corridor-constrained ISAC design substantially enhances the UAV's average communication rate compared with benchmark schemes, demonstrating its effectiveness for environment-adaptive ISAC in distributed low-altitude networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Modelling Quantum Networking with Teleportation.
abstract: We present a simple teleportation-based quantum internet framework with a centralized server architecture. Our model formalizes qubit transfer protocols while using stochastic differential equations to capture entanglement decoherence under both Markovian and non-Markovian noise. We quantify key performance metrics-entanglement generation rate, throughput, and security-validating our predictions through Qiskit simulations. The modular design addresses critical quantum networking challenges: fidelity-latency trade-offs, scalable entanglement distribution, and eavesdropping resilience. Future extensions incorporate multi-hop topologies with quantum repeaters and fault-tolerant error correction, establishing a foundation for scalable quantum networks.

title: DRL-Based Coupling-Aware Secure S-UAV System Leveraging Collaborative Beamforming.
abstract: Small-sized UAVs (S-UAVs) face challenges in secure, energy-efficient data transfer due to limited energy and eavesdropping threats. We propose a collaborative beamforming (CB) system where multiple S-UAVs form a Virtual Antenna Array (VAA) to beamform data to an Edge Server (ES) while nullsteering eavesdroppers, explicitly accounting for mutual coupling (MC) in close formations. The optimization problem of VAA formation is addressed using Multi Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning - Transformer with Bagging(MADRL-T+B), which integrates a Transformer encoder and critic bagging. Simulations study the effect of inter-S-UAV spacing, and path loss on the system and shows the effectiveness of MADRL-T+B algorithm over existing methods in secrecy rate, and energy efficiency, achieving a 5.6 % average improvement in scalability and an average 21 % increase in training stability under high numbers of S-UAVs, and low SNR, respectively.

title: Spectral Efficiency Analysis of Multi-User Pinching-Antenna Systems.
abstract: This paper investigates a multi-user pinching-antenna (PA) system, where a single PA is activated on each waveguide. With the maximum ratio transmission (MRT) beamforming, the system spectral efficiency (SE) is studied, where the inter-user interference term complicates the analysis of the SE. To overcome this obstacle, the stationary phase point method (SPPM) is applied to obtain an analytically tractable form of the SE. The analysis reveals that the average inter-user interference can be negligible with a large waveguide spacing even using the MRT. This insight makes the simple MRT appealing for PA-based multi-user communications. Finally, the theoretical analysis is verified through simulations. Our numerical results confirm that 1) with the aid of SPPM, the approximation of the system SE is accurate; 2) and while increasing the waveguide spacing helps reduce the average inter-user interference, it might degrade the SE due to the increased signal propagation path loss.

title: Detect Error Performance for Satellite Aerial Terrestrial Integrated Cognitive Networks with NOMA and Non-Ideal Limitations.
abstract: Covert transaction (CT) is the popular topic investigated these years. In this research, we study the CT for the satellite aerial terrestrial integrated cognitive networks (SATICNs), particularly, in order to enhance the spectrum efficiency and resource utilization, cognitive technology and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) scheme are used in the SATICNs to improve the system covert performance. Besides, to consider the practical scenarios, the non-ideal hardware, non-ideal channel estimation and the co-channel interferences are also investigated for the SATICNs. In addition, a new defined detection error probability (DEP) is proposed for the CT of the considered system. Furthermore, by considering these factors, the closed-form expression for the DEP is also obtained. Finally, several representative Monte Carlo simulations are derived to evaluate the impacts of system and channel parameters on the covert system performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Feature Importance-Aware Dual-Branch Coding for Task-Oriented Uav Adaptive Transmission.
abstract: Semantic communication is considered a key enabling technology for 6G. However, in UAV scenarios with limited bandwidth and low SNR, conventional single-branch image transmission cannot effectively balance efficiency and task performance. To overcome this, we propose an importanceaware dual-branch joint source-channel coding (I-DBJSCC) framework for UAV semantic image adaptive transmission. The framework incorporates a dual-branch semantic coding (DBSC) module that employs MobileNet and ViT to extract local precision and global consistency features. A gradient-based task activation mapping (Grad-TAM) mechanism is proposed that leverages task-quality feedback to evaluate feature importance, enabling adaptive prioritization of task-relevant information. To optimize transmission under varying channel conditions, we propose a dual-branch joint semantic-channel transmission (DJSCT) mechanism that collaborates with the I-DBJSCC encoder to adaptively select the transmitted semantic features based on available resources. Furthermore, a dual-branch proximal policy optimization (D-PPO) algorithm is proposed to adjust semantic feature transmission ratios. Experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly improves task-oriented semantic spectral efficiency and achieves substantial gains in image reconstruction quality compared with state-of-the-art baselines.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Task-Oriented Semantic Communication for Satellite Remote Sensing Images with Channel Feedback.
abstract: Remote sensing images play a crucial role in many fields such as military reconnaissance and geological exploration. However, the limited bandwidth of satellite-toground communication channels struggles to support massive data transmission. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a task-oriented semantic communication framework for satellite remote sensing images with channel feedback. The proposed transmission framework includes a semantic feature extraction module, a semantic feature selection module, a joint sourcechannel encoding and decoding module, and a task module. The semantic feature extraction module can effectively extract global context features and local detailed features via transformer block and residual blocks, respectively. The semantic feature selection module can select task-relevant features according to signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) obtained from channel feedback. The joint source channel encoding and decoding modules can further improve the transmission robustness. By transmitting task-relevant semantic features while discarding redundant information, our method significantly improves transmission efficiency while preserving downstream-task performance. The extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves higher classification accuracy than state-of-the-art methods on the NWPU-RESISC45 and AID datasets.
