title: Adaptive RIS Control for Mobile mmWave NLoS Communication Using Single-Bit Feedback.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) are emerging as key enablers of reliable industrial automation in the millimeter-wave (mmWave) band, particularly in environments with frequent line-of-sight (LoS) blockage. While prior works have largely focused on theoretical aspects, real-time validation under user mobility remains underexplored. In this work, we propose and experimentally evaluate an adaptive beamforming algorithm that enables RIS reconfiguration via a low-rate feedback link from the mobile user equipment (UE) to the RIS controller, operating without requiring UE position knowledge. The algorithm maintains the received signal power above a predefined threshold using only a single-bit comparison of received power levels. To analyze the algorithm's performance, we establish a simulation-based Monte Carlo (MC) optimization benchmark that assumes full UE position knowledge, accounts for practical hardware constraints, and serves as an upper bound for performance evaluation. Using a hexagonal RIS with 127 elements and 1-bit phase quantization at 23.8 GHz, we validate the proposed approach in a semi-anechoic environment over a$60 \text{cm} \times 92 \text{cm}$area. The results demonstrate that the singlebit feedback-driven algorithm closes much of the performance gap to the MC upper bound while achieving up to 24 dB gain in received power compared to an inactive RIS baseline. These findings highlight the practical potential of feedbackbased adaptive RIS control for robust mmWave non-line-of-sight (NLoS) communication with mobile users.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Scalable Implementation of Adaptive Linear Channel Estimators for OFDM Systems on RF System-on-Chip.
abstract: Accurate channel estimation is essential to establish a reliable wireless connectivity. Traditional estimators such as least squares (LS) offers a low-complexity solution but at the cost of inferior estimation accuracy. Whereas minimum mean square error (MMSE) yields a superior estimate but at the cost of higher complexity. Further, their efficient hardware implementation for real-time baseband processing remains a significant challenge. In this paper, we propose an hardware efficient adaptive channel estimation framework for frame-based orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems, that bridges the performance-complexity trade-off between LS and MMSE estimators. The proposed framework adaptively switches between LS and MMSE estimators based on real-time channel conditions, thereby achieving an optimal balance between estimation accuracy and resource utilization. The framework is implemented on the radio frequency system-on-chip (RFSoC) platform, where we focus on designing custom, AXI4-Stream-compatible cores integrated within the programmable logic (PL) to enable pipelined, high-throughput processing of complex OFDM symbols. Post-synthesis results indicate that the proposed implementation requires approximately 23% less LUTs, 72% less power and 6% lower latency in comparison to MMSE, while delivering the same performance. This hardware-in-the-loop validation confirms the practical viability of the design for future 5G/6G systems, with scalability toward massive MIMO architectures.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Unfolded Hybrid Beamforming for NOMA-Enabled Joint Sensing and Communication.
abstract: We propose integrating Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) into hybrid beamforming (HBF) for JCAS in multi-user scenarios, as an alternative to conventional Spatial Division Multiple Access (SDMA). The framework is analyzed in terms of achievable sum rate, energy efficiency, and beamforming complexity. System performance is optimized for sum rate maximization using Successive Interference Cancellation (SIC) and Deep Unfolding-based optimization, and extended to wideband OFDM systems to support practical broadband 6G networks. Results demonstrate that NOMA-assisted HBF effectively balances efficiency, complexity, and sensing capability. The integration of joint communication and sensing in 6 G can thus transform wireless networks into pervasive intelligent infrastructures, enabling both human-centric and machinedriven applications.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Device-Specific Anomaly Detection Via Transfer Learning in Edge Networks.
abstract: Network anomaly detection is an active research area, with numerous solutions that utilize statistical methods, neural networks, and other machine learning methods. Autoencoders, in particular, have shown great performance by learning representations solely from benign traffic, enabling the detection of zero-day attacks. In this paper, we propose a methodology that uses transfer learning to train autoencoders specifically tailored to individual network devices, thereby improving detection performance over general autoencoder models trained on aggregated network data. Furthermore, benchmarking results indicate that the lightweight device-specific model is suitable for inference on resource-constrained devices, suggesting its feasibility for real-time anomaly detection on edge devices. We compare the device-specific model with the general model by evaluating them against 12 different attack types. The results demonstrate that the proposed method shows promise in improving the anomaly detection performance. The device-specific model outperforms the general model for certain attacks, while achieving similar performance in others.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Joint Rate-Energy Optimization in NOMA BackCom Networks.
abstract: The rapid growth of low-power Internet of things (IoT) devices calls for communication paradigms that jointly ensure spectrum efficiency and energy sustainability. Backscatter communication (BackCom) integrated with non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is a promising enabler, but its performance is tightly coupled to realistic energy harvesting (EH) dynamics and the adaptive control of backscatter nodes (BNs). In this paper, we investigate a NOMA based BackCom uplink system, where multiple EH enabled BNs powered by a dedicated continuous-wave (CW) transmitter, operating under a practical non-linear EH model. To effectively balance the achievable data rates and the battery dynamics of the BNs whose stored energy must also support sensing operations, we formulate the problem as a sequential decision-making task and address it using deep reinforcement learning (DRL). By optimizing the BNs reflection coefficients and power-sharing factors in real time, DRL policies learn to sustain battery levels, prevent energy outages, and maximize throughput across dynamic channel and EH conditions. Comparative evaluation of advanced DRL algorithms, including deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG), prioritized experience replay DDPG (PER-DDPG), combined experience replay DDPG (CER-DDPG), twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3), proximal policy optimization (PPO), soft actor-critic (SAC), and recurrent soft actor-critic (RSAC), demonstrates that off-policy algorithms achieve faster convergence and superior energy-aware sum-rate performance, while linear EH assumptions significantly overestimate system capabilities. The results highlight that DRL-driven optimization offers a robust pathway to practical, self-sustaining NOMA BackCom networks.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Disrupting Multi-Robot Coordination: Strategic Sybil Attack on Exploration Algorithms.
abstract: Cooperative exploration in multi-robot systems is vital for mission-critical tasks such as search and rescue, mine detection, and surveillance. These systems depend on wireless communication, making them susceptible to Sybil attacks, where a single adversarial robot forges multiple fictitious identities to mislead the team. While prior work has largely addressed static or centralized MRS settings, it often neglects the strategic placement of Sybil identities, assuming arbitrary positioning. This paper introduces two novel algorithms for stealthy and effective Sybil robot placement in distributed MRS. We show comparative analysis of random placement and the proposed strategies, and comparatively evaluate both algorithms using distance metrics and their disruptive potential. Furthermore, we design and execute a Sybil attack within a cooperative exploration framework and present extensive simulation-based analysis. Results reveal key vulnerabilities in existing exploration algorithms and emphasize the need for security-aware MRS design.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: DCoRE-QML: Communication-Efficient and Robust Distributed Quantum Machine Learning.
abstract: Distributed quantum computing provides scalability while offering advantages such as enhanced noise mitigation and higher fidelity. Leveraging this, distributed quantum machine learning (DQML) can provide better solutions to practical machine learning (ML) tasks, in contrast to classical ML and single-device QML performance. A key objective in DQML is to reduce inter-node communication costs, thereby enhancing efficiency, accuracy, and mitigating communication-induced noise. Existing communication-optimization approaches are generally application-agnostic and do not address the specific demands of QML circuits-especially quantum neural networks (QNNs), which require iterative training, large input sizes, and gradientbased updates. We propose DCoRE-QML, a framework designed for distributed QML that minimizes communication overhead while accounting for network dynamics (link and node failures) to improve robustness. It employs localized data encoding, delayed weight updates, compression techniques, and persistent entanglement purification to improve performance and fidelity. Experimental results indicate that it outperforms generic state-of-the-art solutions for QNN circuits, with higher fidelity.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Experimental Investigation of Symbol Error Rate in Cost-Effective Full-Duplex RoFSO System.
abstract: This work experimentally demonstrates a cost-effective full-duplex radio-over-free-space optics (FD-RoFSO) system, realized at an overall cost of approximately $ 1600 only, using a commercially available low-cost optical transceiver. The proposed FD-RoFSO setup operates over a shared optical path in a controlled laboratory environment by employing a single pair of collimator lenses to reduce hardware complexity and overall system cost significantly. Higher-order$M$-ary modulation schemes are utilized to enable efficient data transmission by encoding multiple bits per symbol, and a custom-designed frame and phase synchronization algorithm ensures precise post-demodulation error analysis. The symbol error rate (SER) is comprehensively evaluated across different modulation schemes, modulation orders, and data rates, providing a practical and accurate assessment of system performance. Experimental results demonstrate the adaptability of the proposed FD-RoFSO system to various modulation formats and highlight its potential for robust, scalable, and efficient next-generation commercial optical wireless communication.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Bayesian Learning for Sparse Channel Estimation in Underwater Visible Light DCO-OFDM Systems.
abstract: This work introduces a novel framework for channel impulse response (CIR) estimation in sparse multipath environments for direct-current-biased optical OFDM (DCOOFDM) based underwater visible light communication (UVLC) systems, employing Bayesian learning (BL) methods. Initially, the CIR of the UVLC channel is formulated by accounting for absorption and scattering effects. To incorporate turbulence, the CIR is further modulated by a fading coefficient modeled by the lognormal distribution, which effectively captures weak oceanic turbulence. Building upon this, a BL-driven estimation strategy is proposed to exploit the inherent delay-domain sparsity of the multipath CIR in DCO-OFDM UVLC systems. The approach requires only a limited set of pilot subcarriers, thus lowering the pilot overhead compared to conventional channel estimation (CE) schemes. Performance evaluation is carried out using the Oracle-MMSE (O-MMSE) benchmark and the Bayesian Cramer-Rao lower bound (BCRLB). Simulation results confirm that the proposed BL-based estimator, even with reduced pilot requirements, consistently outperforms both classical and sparse CE techniques in terms of normalized mean-square-error (NMSE) and bit error-rate (BER).

title: Unleashing Sensor-Aided Environment Awareness for Beam Management in Beyond-5G Networks: an Openairinterface Experimental Platform.
abstract: Large antenna arrays and beamforming techniques are key components for exploiting the spectrum-rich FR2 bands in next-generation mobile communication networks. Given the site-specific spatio-temporal variations of the mm-wave channel, non-RF sensor inputs and environment awareness can be leveraged to greatly enhance beam management decisions, e.g. via machine learning (ML) techniques. However, the current literature lacks open platforms to gather datasets for the training of such ML techniques and to evaluate novel beam management approaches in real-time, real-world scenarios and full-stack endto-end networks. In this work, we present our SDR-based experimental platform based on OpenAirInterface and are the first to integrate popular low-cost antenna array transceivers, beam sweeping capabilities, and a highly-modular sensor framework and associated interfaces into such a full-stack experimental platform. This enables beam management experimentation in real-world, real-time scenarios and facilitates gathering datasets necessary for developing ML-based beam management protocols that incorporate environment awareness via sensor modalities.

title: Deep Learning Aided Near-Field Beam Prediction for U6G XL-MIMO Multipath Systems.
abstract: The upper-6 GHz (U6G) extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) system is regarded as a promising technology for sixth generation (6 G) systems, whilst it presents inevitable challenges for beam training. The large number of antennas and near-field effect result in high pilot overhead that is not applicable to time-varying scenarios. The existence of multiple paths will also compromise the spectral efficiency (SE) of single-path beamforming schemes. To address these challenges, a DL-aided near-field beam prediction scheme is proposed. A cooperative near-field codebook is designed, while a lightweight multi-task long short-term memory (MT-LSTM) network is established on the user equipment (UE) side. By reserving preceding training results, only a single beam needs to be newly trained in each frame to precisely predict the optimal beamforming vector for near-field multiple-path channels, thus greatly reducing the pilot overhead. Simulation results prove that the proposed scheme can significantly enhance the SE, while requiring only a signal pilot to be trained in each frame.

title: Pinching Beamforming Design for Integrated Sensing and Multicast Communications.
abstract: This paper studies a pinching-antenna system (PASS)-enabled integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework, where pinching beamforming is realized by adaptively adjusting the pinching-antenna (PA) positions along waveguides to simultaneously multicast common information and perform target localization. Specifically, a maxmin fairness (MMF) criterion and the Bayesian Cramer-Rao bound (BCRB) are formulated to quantify the multicasting and sensing performance, respectively. Based on these metrics, a sensing-centric joint design framework is developed to minimize the BCRB subject to multicast quality-of-service (QoS) constraints. A sequential element-wise alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is proposed to efficiently optimize the PA positions for pinching beamforming. Numerical results demonstrate that: (i) the proposed PASSenabled ISAC framework achieves substantially improved sensing accuracy compared with conventional multiple-input multipleoutput (MIMO) schemes while guaranteeing multicast service requirements; and (ii) the localization performance is consistently enhanced as the number of deployed PAs increases.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Movable Antenna-Aided Beamforming and Dual-Scale Mobility Optimization in UAV Systems.
abstract: Integrating movable antennas (MAs) onto an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) unlocks a powerful dual-scale mobility paradigm for enhancing multi-user downlink communications. In this paper, we investigate the joint optimization of base station (BS) active beamforming, macro-scale UAV deployment, and micro-scale MA positioning to maximize the system's sum rate. The formulated non-convex problem is tackled using an alternating optimization (AO) framework that decouples it into three subproblems. Specifically, the fractional programming (FP) technique is leveraged to transform the beamforming subproblem into a standard quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP). For UAV deployment, a successive convex approximation (SCA) based method is developed to optimize its location by managing large-scale channel gains. To address the intricate coupling in MA positioning, we propose a Block Coordinate Descent (BCD) algorithm that iteratively solves a convex surrogate problem for each antenna's position via SCA. Numerical results validate the convergence of our proposed algorithm and demonstrate that exploiting dual-scale mobility significantly enhances the sum rate compared to key benchmarks, including systems with conventional fixed-position antennas (FPAs) and the classic Projected Gradient Ascent (PGA) algorithm.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Latency-Optimized OFDM Systems via Wavelet Transform.
abstract: The evolution of wireless communication systems shifts away from being purely throughput-driven towards embracing additional objectives to broaden the range of applications. Latency is one of those new objectives considered in primary communication standards such as cellular and WiFi. Achieving low system latency requires a latency-focused optimization across all communication layers. A key latency contributor in today's OFDM-based systems is the transmitter- and receiversided Inverse Fourier Transform (IFFT) and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), accounting for up to 20 % of the physical-layer latency. Inherent data dependencies of the FFT algorithm create latency constraints, necessitating the exploration of alternative approaches. In this paper, we investigate an alternative OFDM system based on Wavelet Transform (WT) and Wavelet Packet Transform (WPT) in the realm of low-latency communication and compare its latency as well as hardware complexity against the Fourier Transform baseline. Therefore, accurate latency and area models of the (Inverse) Discrete Wavelet and (Inverse) Discrete Wavelet Packet Transform are presented, all built upon optimized hardware architectures. The resulting quantitative comparison indicates a reduction in the latency-area product of up to 68 % highlighting that WT-based OFDM systems are particularly wellsuited for low-latency applications.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Cancelling Inter-AP-Interference for UL Channel Estimation in Virtual FD CF-mMIMO Systems.
abstract: Cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) systems are being envisioned as an evolution of multi-cell massive MIMO systems, which aim to provide higher spectral and energy efficiencies and facilitate a uniform quality of service (QoS). Recently, CF-mMIMO systems are modeled as a virtual full duplex (vFD) systems, where the access points (APs) independently switch between the uplink and downlink mode to serve all the uplink and downlink users concurrently. This further enhances the overall QoS. However, several issues, like channel estimation, interference suppression, signal detection, etc., need to be addressed to realize such systems. In this work, we focus on devising a strategy for estimating the uplink channel in the presence of concurrent downlink transmissions. For this, we propose an AP mode selection and inter-AP-interference cancellation method to improve the quality of channel estimates, which enhances the signal to interference plus noise ratio, consequently boosts spectral efficiency (SE). Using simulations, we show that the proposed scheme minimizes the normalized mean square error for two pilot assignment schemes, namely, random and user group schemes. The proposed method outperforms with existing method in terms of the average spectral efficiency (SE) for different values of signal-to-noise ratio.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Energy Efficient for Holographic RIS-aided NOMA Near-Field Short-Packet Communication System.
abstract: In this work, we investigate the performance of a holographic reconfigurable intelligent surface (HRIS)-aided downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) network for energy-efficient (EE) short-packet near-field (NF) communications. In particular, we aim to maximize the EE of a multiuser downlink NOMA system by jointly designing the transmit beamforming at the BS and the phase-shift matrix of the HRIS, while explicitly accounting for delay determined by packet size and target packet error probability. Due to the non-convexity of the formulated problem, a sub-optimal iterative solution is developed which efficiently addresses the joint optimization through a combination of alternating optimization (AO), the Dinkelbach method, and successive convex approximation (SCA) techniques. The efficacy and convergence of the proposed algorithm are validated via extensive numerical simulation. Furthermore, we also discuss the impact of key system parameters, such as HRIS reflecting elements, minimum quality of service (QoS) constraints, transmit power budget, and number of users. The potential of HRIS in integration with NOMA, space division multiple access (SDMA), and orthogonal multiple access (OMA), for short packet downlink transmission is demonstrated.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: HF Skywave Massive MIMO Communications with Interference Sparsity-Aware Turbo Receiver.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a low complexity turbo receiver for high frequency (HF) skywave massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. By leveraging the beam based channel model (BBCM), we reveal the interference sparsity of HF skywave massive MIMO systems. Exploiting the interference sparsity, we provide a condition of extracting sufficient observation for signal detection. Motivated by this condition, we construct the interference user terminal (UT) set (IUS) and extract the observation vector from the received signal after matched filtering (MF) for each UT. Then, a low-dimensional interference sparsity-aware detector (ISD) is separately designed for each UT, and the interference sparsity-aware turbo receiver (ISTR) is subsequently formulated using ISDs. Further, we develop an efficient implementation of the ISTR, involving approximate computations of the ISD and the signal reconstructed by ISD. Simulation results confirm that the proposed ISTR achieves excellent performance with relatively low complexity.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: An Eigen-Based High-Precision AoA Estimation for Frequency-Mixing RIS-Assisted Positioning.
abstract: The decoupling feature of frequency-mixing reconfigurable intelligent surface (FMx-RIS) offers a new perspective for channel estimation and positioning in multiple RIS scenarios. This paper proposes a high-precision user equipment (UE) positioning framework using FMx-RIS. By leveraging the frequency-specific “fingerprint” embedded in each reflective path, the proposed method effectively decouples the channels and eliminates path ambiguity. We derive an intrinsic relationship between the received signal and the angle of arrival (AoA), and develop an iterative algorithm that achieves near-CramérRao Bound (CRB) accuracy of angle estimation. Experimental results demonstrate that, with parallel extraction of AoA from multiple UE-RIS links, the framework supports highly precise UE positioning, even in low-SNR regimes.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Transmit and Receive Beamforming Design for Cell-Free ISAC MIMO Systems.
abstract: In this paper, a joint transmit and receive beamforming design for cell-free integrated sensing and communication multi-input multi-output systems is proposed. The dualfunctional base stations (BSs) can simultaneously communicate with downlink users and sense the target of interest, while the effects of line-of-sight links among BSs and self-interference at each BS on the sensing performance are fully taken into account. By adopting the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) as the performance metric for both sensing and communication, we formulate an optimization problem that aims to maximize the sensing SINR subject to communication SINR constraints, a total transmit power constraint, and interference-nulling constraints. To address the resulting non-convex and coupled problem, we develop an alternating optimization algorithm in which the receive beamformer is obtained via null-space projection, whereas the transmit beamformer is computed by reformulating the problem as a semidefinite program and applying semidefinite relaxation. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

title: Sharing Disaster Information Using Mobile Cache at Disaster.
abstract: In recent years, Japan has faced an increasing frequency of large-scale natural disasters. To ensure rapid evacuation and improve survival rates, information on blocked or damaged roads must be promptly shared among evacuees. Delay-Tolerant Networks (DTNs), which enable data exchange via direct communication between mobile devices without relying on infrastructure, offer a promising solution. However, frequent communication in DTNs leads to significant power consumption, which is critical during disasters where battery resources are limited. This study proposes a disaster information-sharing system that designates a subset of devices as Mobile Cache (MC) to actively disseminate data, while others communicate passively to reduce overall energy consumption. Simulation experiments using a Multi-Agent Simulation (MAS) framework evaluate the impact of the proposed approach on evacuation completion rates and total energy consumption.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Block-Level Nonlinear Interference-Exploiting Precoding for PSK: Beyond CI-SLP and CI-BLP.
abstract: This paper investigates constructive interference (CI)-based waveform design for phase-shift keying (PSK) symbols under relaxed block-level power constraints in multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems. Existing linear CI precoding methods, including symbol-level precoding (SLP) and block-level precoding (BLP), are limited by stringent symbol-level power budgets or insufficient block-level degrees of freedom (DoFs). To address these issues, we propose a nonlinear waveform optimization framework that maximizes the minimum CI gain across each block. The optimal waveform is derived in closed form via the Lagrangian function and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions, explicitly expressed with respect to the dual variables. Furthermore, the original problem is reformulated as an equivalent and tractable quadratic programming (QP) problem, and an improved alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm with a linear-time projection scheme is developed to efficiently solve it. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithms outperform conventional CI-SLP and CI-BLP approaches, especially for large block lengths and high-order modulations.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Surplus-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Service Placement in Mobile Edge Computing.
abstract: In a Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) setup, Service Providers (SPs) often do not own the edge infrastructure, since it is managed by independent Infrastructure Providers (IPs). This separation requires economic negotiation for service placement under resource and cost constraints, involving dynamic coordination between the SP and the IP with asymmetric information and differing goals. Centralized or static models fail to capture strategic behavior and private preferences, making negotiationbased approaches essential. We model MEC placement as a finite-horizon bargaining game and implement a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) framework. The SP learns dynamic pricing under partial observability, whereas IPs follow various concession strategies. To encourage fair and efficient agreements, we apply reward shaping based on a Nash-log-based surplus with time decay, along with a demand-aware feasibility filter that excludes economically infeasible negotiations. Experiments on real MEC traces show that our method increases the SP surplus by 29.2 %, increases the agreement rate by 9.8 % and lowers the negotiated prices by 35 %, while converging in fewer rounds. These results show that our reinforcement learning (RL) based bargaining approach provides a scalable and adaptive solution for decentralized MEC placement under behavioral and economic uncertainty.

title: Standard Condition Number-Based Robust Signal Detection with Whitening under Uncertainty.
abstract: Robust signal detection in colored noise with unknown covariance is essential in radar, cognitive radio, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), and quantum sensing applications. This paper develops a unified analytical framework for the Standard Condition Number (SCN) detector, which employs the ratio of the largest to smallest eigenvalues of the whitened sample covariance matrix. The framework jointly covers both ideal conditions in which the training and sensing noise statistics are identical and disturbed conditions in which interference or jamming alters the sensing covariance. Despite the SCN's practical relevance, its finite-sample false-alarm and detection behavior has not been analytically characterized. Using random matrix theory (RMT), we derive general expressions for these probabilities, provide closed-form results for special cases, and show that the SCN preserves the Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) property under covariance mismatch. Analytical and simulation results confirm that the proposed unified framework delivers consistent detection performance and greater robustness than conventional eigenvalue- and LRT-based detectors.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Learning Augmented Wireless Channel Estimation: Over the Air Training and Validation.
abstract: Deep learning (DL) based wireless physical layer (PHY) has been shown to outperform conventional PHY, especially when trained using appropriate synthetic datasets or when mathematical modelling of the wireless environment is complex. However, training DL PHY using real radio signals (real dataset) is challenging since the channel impulse response is unknown. In this work, we develop an end-to-end training and validation framework for the DL-based PHY using software-defined radio (SDR). We demonstrate the significance of real-dataset-based training for wireless PHY performance and explore a fine-tuning approach to address the limited availability of real datasets. For resource-constrained edge platforms used for PHY deployment, we proposed a novel augmentation approach where we augment conventional baseband signal processing with lightweight DL. Experimental results using the SDR testbed show that finetuning DL-based receivers with limited OTA data significantly improves real-world generalisation. Compared to state-of-theart end-to-end DL PHY, the proposed approach reduces the number of parameters by 85 % and multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations by 99 %, improves inference speed by eight times, and is modulation-agnostic. Further, the proposed approach offers up to 40 % higher throughout.

title: Adaptive Hybrid RF/FSO Uplink Design for HAP-Assisted UAV Networks.
abstract: This paper investigates a cooperative two-hop uplink architecture for multi-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications, where a high-altitude platform (HAP) acts as a relay between UAVs and a ground station through hybrid radio frequency (RF) and free-space optical (FSO) links. To enhance link reliability under weather-dependent FSO degradation, a dynamic adaptive combining (DAC) mechanism is introduced to jointly exploit FSO and sub-THz channels on the HAPground backhaul. An integrated optimization framework is developed to maximize the overall hybrid RF/FSO capacity while ensuring fairness among multiple UAVs. The framework simultaneously optimizes UAV trajectories, bandwidth and power allocation, HAP transmit power distribution, and DAC coefficients under stringent backhaul and energy constraints. The resulting formulation is highly nonlinear and nonconvex due to coupled trajectory and resource variables. To address this, an inner-approximation (IA) algorithm is proposed, which iteratively convexifies the problem and guarantees convergence to a stationary solution. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms conventional selection combining and hard-switching baselines, achieving higher throughput and robustness across diverse atmospheric and mission conditions.

title: Joint Transceiver and Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Design in mmWave MU-MISO Systems with Hardware Impairment and Imperfect CSI.
abstract: This paper investigates a millimeter-wave (mmWave) multiuser multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) transceiver system assisted by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). Furthermore, potential hardware impairments (HWI) and imperfect channel state information (CSI) are considered in the system model, reflecting realistic implementation constraints. The objective is to achieve user fairness, and thus reduce inequality among users, by jointly optimizing the transceiver beamforming and discrete RIS phase shifts to minimize the worst-case mean square error (MSE) across all users, thereby strictly ensuring user fairness. To solve this non-convex min-max problem, we develop an alternating optimization (AO)-based algorithm that iteratively decouples the coupled variables, enabling tractable and efficient subproblem solutions. Simulations demonstrate rapid convergence within 31 iterations and up to 15% worst-case MSE reduction compared to benchmarks.

title: A Cross-Layer Protocol for Missing Tag Identification Under Probabilistic Cloning Attacks in Large-Scale RFID Systems.
abstract: Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) serves as a core technology in Internet of Things (IoT) applications such as retail management, industrial warehousing, and object tracking. Accurately identifying missing tags in such systems is essential to prevent economic loss and protect information security. However, existing identification protocols perform poorly under probabilistic cloning attacks, in which counterfeit tags intermittently impersonate missing genuine tags. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes the Missing Tag Identification Under Probabilistic Cloning Attacks (MPCA) protocol, a cross-layer protocol for missing tag identification under probabilistic cloning attacks. MPCA dynamically chooses between two response modes by precomputing and comparing their average execution time. Then it employs a marker vector to assign and filter slots for tags, and introduces differentiated response strategies to reduce time overhead. Furthermore, MPCA leverages physical-layer signal analysis via an enhanced DBSCAN algorithm to resolve collision slots into parallel identification opportunities by accurately estimating the number of concurrent tag responses. We provide rigorous theoretical analysis to derive optimal parameters that balance execution efficiency and identification reliability. Extensive simulations demonstrate that MPCA can maintain required identification reliability while reducing execution time by up to 50.9% compared to state-of-the-art protocols.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Multi-Agent Sac Enabled Beamforming Design for Joint Secret Key Generation and Data Transmission.
abstract: Physical layer key generation (PLKG) has emerged as a promising solution for achieving highly secured and lowlatency key distribution, offering information-theoretic security that is inherently resilient to quantum attacks. However, simultaneously ensuring a high data transmission rate and a high secret key generation rate under eavesdropping attacks remains a major challenge. In time-division duplex (TDD) systems with multiple antennas, we derive closed-form expressions for both rates by modeling the legitimate channel as a time-correlated autoregressive (AR) process. This formulation leads to a highly nonconvex and time-coupled optimization problem, rendering traditional optimization methods ineffective. To address this issue, we propose a multi-agent soft actor-critic (SAC) framework equipped with a long short-term memory (LSTM) adversary prediction module to cope with the partial observability of the eavesdropper's mode. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior performance compared with other benchmark algorithms, while effectively balancing the trade-off between secret key generation rate and data transmission rate. The results also confirm the robustness of the proposed framework against intelligent eavesdropping and partial observation uncertainty.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Enhancing Secret Key Generation for UAV Communications via Codeword Reconstruction.
abstract: With the rapid advancement of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), ensuring the security of communication links among UAVs has become crucial. In this paper, we propose a novel physical layer key generation scheme based on channel codeword reconstruction. In UAV communications, the high mobility of aerial nodes leads to short channel coherence time, which together with noise causes inevitable channel estimation errors. These errors significantly degrades the performance of wireless channel-based key generation. Therefore, we propose a codeword construction algorithm that achieves a polarization characteristic, which effectively segregates reliable keys from unreliable ones. Compared to the existing quantization-based key generation scheme, our approach maximize the utilization of raw channel information and employ soft-decision decoding to generate key. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme reduces the key disagreement rate for legitimate users and increases the number of consistently generated keys. Furthermore, our method ensures a lower key consistency rate for eavesdropper, which guarantees system security.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Novel User Authentication Scheme Via Led Spectral Fingerprinting.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel authentication method based on the spectral fingerprint characteristics of light-emitting diode (LED). The spectral fingerprint of LED originating from manufacturing process variations is analyzed. A method for constructing a simple spectrometer is presented, and its measurement accuracy is verified to meet the identification precision requirements, enabling it to replace large and expensive professional spectral measurement equipment. A multi-stage support vector machine (SVM) classification algorithm based on feature extraction combined with mathematical modeling is proposed. A mathematical model of the spectral profile is established using a combination of Gaussian and asymmetric Lorentzian functions. Several key shape features are extracted from the spectral profile through function fitting. These features are then used to train one-class SVM. Employing a multi-stage structure and anomaly detection, the proposed method achieves an overall accuracy of 98.4 %, a precision of 100 %, and a recall rate of 97.8 %. Compared with an algorithm based on neural networks, the proposed method maintains high accuracy while featuring a simpler algorithmic structure, lower resource consumption, faster inference, and better physical interpretability.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Compressed Multiband Sensing in FR3 Using Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers.
abstract: Joint detection and localization of users and scatterers in multipath-rich channels on multiple bands is critical for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in 6G. Existing multiband sensing methods are limited by classical beamforming or computationally expensive approaches. This paper introduces alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM)-assisted compressed multiband sensing (CMS), hereafter referred to as ADMM-CMS, which is a novel framework for multiband sensing using uplink quadrature amplitude modulation-modulated pilot symbols. To solve the CMS problem, we develop an adaptive ADMM algorithm that adjusts to noise and ensures automatic stopping if converged. ADMM combines the decomposability of dual ascent with the robustness of augmented Lagrangian methods, making it suitable for large-scale structured optimization. Simulations show that ADMM-CMS achieves higher spatial resolution and improved denoising compared to Bartlett-type beamforming, yielding a 34 dB gain in per-antenna transmit power for achieving a 0.9 successful recovery probability (SRP). Moreover, compared to performing compressed sensing separately on the constituent 7 GHz and 10 GHz sub-bands, ADMM-CMS achieves reductions in delay root mean squared error of 34.46% and 40.76%, respectively, at -41 dBm per-antenna transmit power, while also yielding improved SRP. Our findings demonstrate ADMM-CMS as an efficient enabler of ISAC in frequency range 3 (FR3, 7-24 GHz) for 6G systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Computation-Efficient Multi-Scale Multi-Granularity Framework for Mobile Traffic Forecasting Via Hierarchical Coherence.
abstract: With emerging infrastructure paradigms such as AI-RAN, next-generation mobile networks are expected to support unprecedented user density and transmission speeds. The resulting massive mobile traffic necessitates real-time prediction at base stations (BSs), enabling a wide range of optimization tasks essential for network efficiency, including anomaly detection, resource allocation, and congestion control. Achieving accurate predictions requires integrating both global trend dependencies and local temporal variations in traffic streams. However, the limited computational resources at BSs are insufficient to support high-capacity models that process long-scale and fine-grained time series while maintaining low latency. To address this bottleneck, we propose MSMG, a Multi-Scale and Multi-Granularity framework for mobile traffic forecasting. MSMG aggregates traffic measurements at multiple levels, each handled by a distinct predictor: upper levels capture coarsegrained but long-term dependencies, while lower levels preserve fine-grained but short-term variations. This hierarchical design allows MSMG to flexibly assign suitable models to each level, thereby reducing average computational cost while maintaining predictive accuracy. To reconcile these heterogeneous predictors into a holistic view of mobile traffic, we exploit hierarchical coherence-an intrinsic structure across aggregation levels. We formulate this coherence as a conditional optimization problem w.r.t. the predictors' outputs and solve a reconciled forecast. We further transform this optimization into a differentiable module that supports consistent gradient flow, which enables joint forecasting and reconciliation in an end-to-end manner. Extensive evaluations on a public mobile traffic dataset demonstrate the superiority of the proposed framework.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: ReaLM: Real-Time Channel Prediction with Distilled LLM.
abstract: In the realm of next-generation wireless communications, real-time and accurate channel state information (CSI) prediction remains a major challenge due to the complex, dynamic, and noise-prone nature of wireless environments. To tackle these difficulties, we propose ReaLM, an efficient framework that adapts and compresses large language models for channel prediction tasks. We fine-tune the Llama model with a time-frequency data fusion feature extraction module, enabling more effective spatiotemporal sequence modeling of CSI. After training, we design a knowledge distillation strategy to reduce the high computational latency and heavy parameter load of large language models, compressing the model by 62% and accelerating inference by 58%. During training, we apply data augmentation and noise injection to improve the model's antiinterference capability. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ReaLM outperforms traditional baselines in low-SNR and crossenvironment scenarios, establishing itself as a robust and efficient solution for 6G real-time channel prediction.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Secrecy Energy Efficiency Maximization for RIS-Assisted UAV-MEC Networks: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Approach.
abstract: The unmanned aerial vehicle carrying mobile edge computing server (UAV-MEC) is expected to provide strong computational capability, reliable and flexible connectivity, and high adaptability to ground networks. Reducing energy consumption and improving information secrecy are severe challenges faced by emerging wireless communication systems. In this work, we investigate a secrecy energy efficiency (SEE) maximization problem in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) assisted UAV-MEC networks by jointly optimizing the RIS phase shift, UAV trajectory, UAV cruising time, and the ground user (GU) scheduling. The block coordinate descent (BCD) approach is used to convert the optimization problem into two tractable subproblems, which can be solved by the Dinkelbach algorithm and the double deep Q-network (DDQN), respectively. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly improves the secrecy energy efficiency compared to benchmark methods.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Semantic Inference Over the Air: An Efficient Task-Oriented Communication System.
abstract: Empowered by deep learning, semantic communication marks a paradigm shift from transmitting raw data to conveying task-relevant meaning, enabling more efficient and intelligent wireless systems. In this study, we explore a deep learning-based task-oriented communication framework that jointly considers classification performance, computational latency, and communication cost. We evaluate ResNets-based models on the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets to simulate real-world classification tasks in wireless environments. We partition the model at various points to simulate split inference across a wireless channel. By varying the split location and the size of the transmitted semantic feature vector, we systematically analyze the trade-offs between task accuracy and resource efficiency. Experimental results show that, with appropriate model partitioning and semantic feature compression, the system can retain over 85\% of baseline accuracy while significantly reducing both computational load and communication overhead.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Uncertainty-Aware Bi-Level Robust Beamforming Optimization for 6G Cell-Free RAN.
abstract: In this paper, we study the robust downlink beamforming for cell-free networks through a bi-level scheme, where the upper level maximizes the network worst-case user rate, while the lower level selects channel estimation errors within a bounded uncertainty set to minimize users' signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratios (SINRs). To enable tractable design, we derive the closed-form worst case bounds for both the desired-signal and multi-user interference terms, and collapse the bi-level program into a tractable single-level reformulation that admits an outer loop search for one-dimensional SINR with inner loop for second-order cone programming (SOCP) feasibility checks that provides strong robustness guarantees. We also propose a low-complexity bi-level adversarial projected-gradient (BAPG) method that directly updates the beamformers using adversarial CSI selections, achieving a favorable robustness and complexity trade-off. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed methods consistently outperform the baseline MRT method under CSI errors, with an improvement of the worst-case max-min rate by 119.6% on average, while also reduces the running time by over two orders of magnitude.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Integrated Sensing and Semantic Communication with Adaptive Source-Channel Coding.
abstract: Semantic communication has emerged as a new paradigm to facilitate the performance of integrated sensing and communication systems in 6G. However, most of the existing works mainly focus on sensing data compression to reduce the subsequent communication overheads, without considering the integrated transmission framework for both the SemCom and sensing tasks. This paper proposes an adaptive source-channel coding and beamforming design framework for integrated sensing and SemCom systems by jointly optimizing the coding rate for SemCom task and the transmit beamforming for both the SemCom and sensing tasks. Specifically, an end-to-end semantic distortion function is approximated by deriving an upper bound composed of source and channel coding induced components, and then a hybrid Cramér-Rao bound (HCRB) is also derived for target position under imperfect time synchronization. To facilitate the joint optimization, a distortion minimization problem is formulated by considering the HCRB threshold, channel uses, and power budget. Subsequently, an alternating optimization algorithm composed of successive convex approximation and fractional programming is proposed to address this problem by decoupling it into two subproblems for coding rate and beamforming designs, respectively. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed scheme outperforms the conventional deep joint source-channel coding-water filling-zero forcing benchmark.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: ISAC-Enabled Covert Communications Under Sensing-Specific CSI.
abstract: Given that the acquisition of warder-related channel state information (CSI) is challenging but critical for covert communication system design, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) technology presents a promising pathway to address this issue. In this work, an ISAC-enabled covert communication architecture is proposed, where the location of the warder is estimated and the sensing-specific CSI is characterized for beamforming optimization. Specifically, the sensing results exhibit a deterministic impact on covert communication, establishing a fundamental coupling between sensing and covert communication functions. Besides, the sensing accuracy performance and the transmission covertness performance are analyzed for the subsequent system design. Further, a weighted optimization problem is formulated for achieving improved trade-offs between communication and sensing performance. This non-convex problem is solved by the sequential convex approximation-based algorithm, where the lossy$\mathcal{S}$-procedure is employed to handle the location uncertainty. Simulation results validate the superiority of the proposed scheme over various benchmarks. Furthermore, there exists an optimal communication-sensing weighting factor that maximizes the covert rate.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Optimal Transmit Beamforming for MIMO ISAC with Unknown Target and User Locations.
abstract: This paper studies a challenging scenario in a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system where the locations of the sensing target and the communication user are both unknown and random, while only their probability distribution information is known. In this case, how to fully utilize the spatial resources by designing the transmit beamforming such that both sensing and communication can achieve satisfactory performance statistically is a difficult problem, which motivates the study in this paper. Moreover, we aim to reveal if it is desirable to have similar probability distributions for the target and user locations in terms of the ISAC performance. Firstly, based on only probability distribution information, we establish communication and sensing performance metrics via deriving the expected rate or posterior Cramér-Rao bound (PCRB). Then, we formulate the transmit beamforming optimization problem to minimize the PCRB subject to the expected rate constraint, for which the optimal solution is derived. It is unveiled that the rank of the optimal transmit covariance matrix is upper bounded by the summation of MIMO communication channel matrices for all possible user locations. Furthermore, due to the need to cater to multiple target/user locations, we investigate whether dynamically employing different beamforming designs over different time slots improves the performance. It is proven that using a static beamforming strategy is sufficient for achieving the optimal performance. Numerical results validate our analysis, show that ISAC performance improves as the target/user location distributions become similar, and provide useful insights on the BS-target/user association strategy.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Block-Sparsity-Aware Message Passing Algorithm for Wavenumber-Domain Holographic MIMO Channel Estimation.
abstract: In this paper, we study the channel estimation (CE) of holographic multiple-input multiple-output (HMIMO) systems in non-line-of-sight (NLoS) environments, and propose an efficient message passing-based CE method by utilizing the block-sparsity of the equivalent wavenumber-domain (WD) channel. Concretely, based on the quantization of cluster centers, a probabilistic model is first presented to capture the blocksparsity in the lattice ellipses of plane wave at the transceiver and thus in the 2D WD channel matrix. Then, the hybrid generalized approximate message passing (GAMP) algorithm is employed to estimate the channel, where a carefully-designed message passing module is incorporated into the GAMP module to handle the block-sparsity. Finally, simulation results are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed CE algorithm.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Covertness Analysis in LEO Mega Constellations.
abstract: The aggregated interference from co-channel satellites in low earth orbit (LEO) mega constellations provides a shield to prevent signal detection by adversaries. In this paper, we propose an analytical framework to evaluate the fundamental covertness performance against the eavesdropper in LEO mega constellations with the aid of stochastic geometry. Specifically, the probability distribution of the interference power is first obtained via its Laplace transform, and then the covert probability is derived to characterize the transmission covertness. The results show an explicit relationship between the minimum covert probability and the transmit powers of satellite transmitter and interfering satellites, and reveal that the increasing altitude of the eavesdropper decreases the minimum covert probability.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Trajectory and Beamforming Design for Secure UAV Relay Communication Via Constrained Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) play a critical role in modern wireless communication systems. This study addresses the secrecy rate optimization problem in a UAVassisted relay system, where a UAV serves as a mobile relay to amplify and forward (AF) confidential information. To ensure quality of service (QoS) for legitimate users, a minimum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) threshold is introduced. However, these constraints significantly increase the complexity of the optimization problem. To tackle this challenge, we model the problem as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP) and propose a solution using the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm augmented with a Lagrangian multiplier mechanism (SAC-Lag). This approach effectively learns cost functions to satisfy the constraints while optimizing the secrecy rate. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed scheme outperforms benchmark algorithms by maintaining a high average secrecy rate and substantially reducing the duration of SINR constraint violations.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Distributed Beamforming Design for User SINR Fairness in LEO Multi-Satellite Cooperative Systems.
abstract: Thanks to their seamless global coverage and highly flexible inter-satellite cooperation, cooperative Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations have emerged as a cornerstone for achieving ubiquitous 6G connectivity and represent a prominent research frontier in satellite communications. This paper studies a LEO multi-satellite cooperative downlink communication system. The system comprises multiple LEO satellites, all of which non-coherently transmit to all users located within the service region. In this setup, our objective is to maximize the minimum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) at users, subject to the transmit power constraints at the satellites. Firstly, we propose a centralized precoding design based on a successive convex approximation (SCA). By introducing auxiliary variables, we transform the non-convex parts of the original problem into convex ones via Taylor approximation. On this basis, we combine the framework of SCA with alternative direction method of multipliers (ADMM) to design a distributed algorithm. Through simulations, we demonstrate that our designed distributed algorithm yields nearly identical optimal solutions to the centralized algorithm, all while achieving SINR fairness across users.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Diffusion-Driven Learning Framework for Enhanced Predictive Channel Modeling in 6G Wireless Communications.
abstract: To overcome the limitations of spatially sparse channel measurements and the poor generalization of conventional predictive models, this paper proposes a prior-enhanced predictive framework that integrates generative augmentation and prior-guided prediction within a unified architecture. We propose a space-time-frequency (STF) diffusion algorithm that generates synthetic channel data while preserving key statistical characteristics. Then we focus on a novel prior-aware prediction module that operates on a low-dimensional manifold extracted from measured channel state information. An innovative composite learning scheme is introduced, in which diffusion-generated structural priors are fused into the predictive pipeline, raising the accuracy limit of prediction and significantly improving robustness across diverse channel environments. Extensive experiments on real-world channel measurements further validate our approach, demonstrating its strong potential for advanced wireless communication systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Covertness and Secrecy Design for Wireless Communications Under Active Attacks.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the covertness and secrecy of wireless communications under an active attacker scenario, where attackers perform simultaneous detection/eavesdropping and jamming. To guarantee the covertness and secrecy of transmissions, both detection and eavesdropping attacks are mitigated using physical layer security techniques. To depict the covertness and secrecy performance of the system, we model the covertness outage probability and the secrecy outage probability, and then analytically characterize the optimal covert secrecy rate (CSR) under an artificial noise (AN)-based transmission scheme. Extensive numerical results demonstrate the achievable CSR performance and reveal the impact of active attacks on system security in the context of the AN-based scheme.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: DEEL: Diffusion-Enhanced Energy and Latency Trade-Off for Low-Altitude Emergency Networks.
abstract: In post-disaster scenarios where terrestrial infrastructure is destroyed, Low-Altitude Emergency Networks, which are a critical application of Low-Altitude Intelligent Networks (LAIN), offer a rapidly deployable and resilient solution. Leveraging their mobility and Line-of-Sight (LoS) capabilities, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) serve as essential nodal platforms. However, their operation face a fundamental trade-off between limited battery endurance and stringent low-latency service demands. Existing studies often optimize energy efficiency and latency reduction separately or rely on rigid linear weighting schemes, limiting adaptability. To address this, we jointly optimize UAV trajectories, task allocation, and resource management using a multi-objective multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework enhanced by a Generative Diffusion Model. This integration enables efficient exploration in high-dimensional, dynamic environments, producing Pareto-optimal policies that balance energy consumption and delay. Simulations demonstrate superior convergence stability, strong adaptability to diverse operational preferences, and a substantial system cost reduction of up to 62.68%.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Towards Native Intelligence: 6G-LLM Trained with Reinforcement Learning from NDT Feedback.
abstract: Owing to its comprehensive understanding of upperlayer application requirements and the capabilities of practical communication systems, the 6G-LLM (6G domain large language model) offers a promising pathway toward realizing network native intelligence. Serving as the system orchestrator, the 6G-LLM drives a paradigm shift that fundamentally departs from existing rule-based approaches, which primarily rely on modular, experience-driven optimization. By contrast, the 6G-LLM substantially enhances network flexibility and adaptability. Nevertheless, current efforts to construct 6G-LLMs are constrained by their reliance on large-scale, meticulously curated, humanauthored corpora, which are impractical to obtain in real-world scenarios. Moreover, purely offline-trained models lack the capacity for continual self-improvement, limiting their ability to adapt to the highly dynamic requirements of wireless communication environments. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel training paradigm termed RLDTF (Reinforcement Learning from Digital Twin Feedback) for 6G-LLMs. This framework leverages network digital twins to generate reward signals based on orchestration outcomes, while employing reinforcement learning to guide the model toward optimal decision-making dynamically. Furthermore, we introduce a weighted token mechanism to improve output accuracy. Comprehensive experimental results demonstrate that our proposed framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in orchestration accuracy and solution optimality.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Ray Antenna Array Enhanced Low-Altitude ISAC: Performance Analysis and Beamforming Design.
abstract: The low-altitude economy (LAE) heavily relies on aerial vehicles, yet these platforms remain vulnerable to environmental and security risks, necessitating robust airspace monitoring. Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) as one of the key technologies of 6G provides potential solutions for safe LAE. However, conventional antenna arrays face limitations in cost, scalability, and coverage, especially directly above the base station, due to hardware complexity and degraded angular resolution. By exploiting the recently proposed ray antenna array (RAA), this paper considers a RAA-enhanced low-altitude ISAC system. RAA architecture employs multiple ray-arranged arrays directly connected without phase shifters, significantly reducing hardware costs while supporting flexible beamforming via dynamic ray selection. Moreover, RAA can provide uniform angular resolution and eliminates coverage holes, making it particularly suitable for low-altitude ISAC. In this paper, we formulate an optimization problem for joint ray selection and beamforming to enhance sensing coverage under communication constraints. An efficient alternating optimization algorithm is proposed to solve this problem. Analytical and simulation results demonstrate that RAA achieves higher sensing signal-to-noise ratio compared to traditional arrays, offering a cost-effective and high-performance solution for achieving low-altitude ISAC.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: In-Orbit Collaborative Computing Method for Real-Time Tasks in Low Earth Orbit Satellite Networks.
abstract: With the rapid evolution of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite Internet, onboard intelligent applications impose increasingly stringent requirements on real-time task processing capability. However, a systematic theoretical basis for determining the minimum collaborative computing resources required to satisfy given reliability constraints is still lacking. To address this issue, this paper proposes a modeling and analytical framework for inorbit collaborative computing of real-time tasks. A dual-layer satellite architecture with functional separation is considered, where one layer is responsible for remote sensing and task triggering, while the other layer provides distributed computing resources for collaborative processing. By integrating a marked Poisson point process, a coupling model between collaborative node scale and spatial beam coverage is established. Based on Amdahl's law, a parallel processing model is then developed to characterize the relationship between collaborative node count and task latency. Closed-form expressions for the minimum required number of collaborative nodes and the corresponding optimal satellite search radius under quality-of-service constraints are derived. Monte Carlo simulations validate the accuracy of the proposed model. The results quantitatively characterize the relationship between task reliability requirements and satellite parameters, providing theoretical support for resource planning and rapid resource bounding in satellite networks.

title: SAASN: A Spatially-Aware Adaptive Scheduling Network for Large-Scale Multi-UAV Tasking.
abstract: Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has emerged as a potent paradigm for large-scale multi-UAV task scheduling. However, existing frameworks often suffer from static architectures lacking adaptive reasoning and inefficient, fixed-rhythm training strategies. To address this, we introduce the Spatially-Aware Adaptive Scheduling Network (SAASN), a hierarchical DRL framework overcoming these limitations via synergistic, adaptive mechanisms. First, we design a novel allocator featuring a Global-Local Fusion Gate, which dynamically arbitrates between sparse local attention and dense global attention to enable a more robust and flexible spatial representation. Second, we enhance the planner with a Value-Weighted Depotcentric Context Module, imbuing the agent with an economic awareness that leads to more profitable routing decisions. Finally, we develop an advanced Policy Diagnosis-driven Asynchronous Training Curriculum (PSATS), which intelligently governs the hierarchical learning process by diagnosing the allocator's policy state to trigger the planner's training asynchronously and to dynamically adapt training parameters. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SAASN establishes a new state-of-the-art, significantly outperforming strong baselines in solution quality and training efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Beamforming and Time-Slot Allocation for Spectrum Sharing in Integrated Satellite-Terrestrial Networks.
abstract: The integration of satellite and terrestrial networks can provide ubiquitous connectivity and efficient spectrum utilization. This paper investigates a spectrum sharing scenario for satellite and terrestrial downlinks. Terrestrial users (TUs) are directly served by small base stations (SBSs) and coexist with satellite users (SUs) under a time division multiple access (TDMA) protocol. To address the severe co-channel interference between satellite and terrestrial transmissions, we formulate a joint beamforming and time slot scheduling problem, aiming to maximize the weighted sum rates of the SU and TU. This problem is highly non-convex due to the coupling between the continuous beamforming vectors and the discrete scheduling variables. To address this challenge, we develop an alternating optimization framework. Specifically, the beamforming subproblem is solved via successive convex approximation (SCA) and second-order cone (SOC) reformulation, while the time slot scheduling subproblem is addressed via integer linear programming (ILP). Simulation results demonstrate that this approach significantly improves the achievable sum rate compared to traditional schemes while ensuring fairness between satellite and terrestrial users.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: NLOS-Identified RSS Localization via Enzyme Action Optimization.
abstract: With the continuous advancement of the 6th generation (6G) communication technology, the demand for locationbased services (LBS) has become critical. As a mainstream technique in wireless localization, received signal strength (RSS) localization has received significant attention. However, most existing RSS-based methods cannot obtain effective positioning in non-line-of-sight (NLOS) environments due to the multipath effect. In this paper, a new NLOS-identified RSS positioning method via Enzyme Action Optimization (EAO) is proposed. We first derive a signal detection theory-based NLOS identification criterion by leveraging multiple RSS measurements. Depending on the prior probabilities information, the Generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) and Neyman-Pearson (NP) criterion are respectively adopted to derive the decision criterion. Then, we propose an EAO-based RSS (EAO-RSS) positioning algorithm. The algorithm mimics the binding and catalytic processes of enzymes with substrates to dynamically adjust candidate estimates in search of the global optimum. As a result, accurate RSS-based localization can be achieved under NLOS condition. Simulation results show that the proposed method can improve positioning accuracy by more than 3.85% compared with the state-of-the-art.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Fluid Antenna-Enhanced Flexible Beamforming.
abstract: Fluid antenna systems encompass a broad class of reconfigurable antenna technologies that offer substantial spatial diversity for various optimization objectives and communication tasks. Their capability to enhance spatial resolution within a fixed physical aperture makes fluid antennas particularly attractive for next-generation wireless deployments. In this work, we focus on the beamforming problem using a two-dimensional planar fluid antenna array. Since both narrow-beam and broad-beam patterns are essential in practical communication networks, enabling flexible beamforming through fluid antennas becomes an important and interesting research direction. We establish a unified and flexible framework that connects arbitrary beam-pattern synthesis with fluid-antenna port selection. The resulting formulation transforms beam-pattern reconstruction into a sparse regression problem, which is addressed using a tailored compressive sensing algorithm designed to operate efficiently with the fast Fourier transform (FFT). Furthermore, to ensure physically consistent phase modeling in the desired beam, we introduce an iterative FFT-based phase retrieval method. Owing to its structure, the proposed phase-refinement procedure exhibits low computational complexity and rapid convergence, requiring only one FFT and one inverse FFT per iteration. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed flexible beamforming framework. Compared with conventional fixed-array architectures, fluid antennas exhibit significantly improved beam-pattern reconstruction accuracy, highlighting their potential for high-resolution and adaptive beamforming in future wireless systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Semantic Communication-Enabled Cooperative BEV Semantic Segmentation Frame in Internet of Vehicles.
abstract: The precision of Bird's Eye View (BEV) semantic segmentation directly affects the decision-making reliability of autonomous driving systems. However, existing methods encounter significant challenges in feature redundancy suppression, channel robustness enhancement, and multi-vehicle feature alignment. To tackle these issues, this paper presents a Semantic Communication-Enabled Cooperative BEV Semantic Segmentation Framework (SCC-BEVSS). First, we establish a variational optimization objective grounded in Information Bottleneck (IB) theory to extract compact semantic features from multi-view images, effectively reducing feature redundancy in BEV representations. Second, a Joint Source-Channel Coding (JSCC) scheme is designed to ensure reliable transmission of semantic features under IoV low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. Finally, we introduce a multi-level feature fusion mechanism that incorporates a feature space calibration module and an attention enhancement module to address spatial misalignment issues in multi-vehicle cooperation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework surpasses existing methods with notable gains in mean Intersection over Union (mIoU).
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Analytical Modeling of Energy Consumption for a LoRaWAN Class B Node.
abstract: This paper proposes an analytical model to evaluate the energy consumption of a Class B end node (EN) in LoRaWAN, a low-power wide-area network (LPWAN) standard. Based on the state transitions of Class B nodes, the current consumption and duration of each state are defined to estimate the daily energy consumption. A theoretical expression is then derived to estimate the battery lifetime of the EN as a function of parameters such as initial battery capacity, spreading factor, beacon period, and ping-slot interval. The formulation inherently includes Class A operation, which is mandatory for ENs. Numerical analyses are conducted to evaluate the impact of various Class B-related parameters on the EN's lifetime. Furthermore, when the Class B cycle becomes sufficiently long -effectively disabling downlink operation- the results converge to those of Class A, confirming the validity of the derived expression.
