title: SWIPT with Probabilistic Amplitude Shaping of 5G LDPC Coded Modulation.
abstract: In this paper, we present theoretical analyses and a new scheme for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT). From the information theory perspective, we define the infinite-length energy-information (E-I) region for the power splitting-based SWIPT system with finite-alphabet inputs. Moreover, we also define the finite-length E-I region and derive the lower bound on the upper boundary (capacity) by the derived random coding bound (RCB) for SWIPT. For practical coded modulation, we propose a new SWIPT scheme based on the probabilistic amplitude shaping (PAS) with low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. In this scheme, the constant composition distribution matcher (CCDM) of the PAS is employed to adjust the distribution of channel inputs to enable wireless power transfer (WPT), while the 5G LDPC code is employed to support reliable wireless information transfer (WIT). Simulation results show that: 1) the proposed SWIPT scheme with 5 G LDPC coded PAS closely approaches the lower bound of the finite-length capacity; 2) the proposed SWIPT scheme can achieve more than 20 % improvement of the power transfer performance over the conventional bit-interleaved coded modulation (BICM) scheme.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Two-Timescale Uplink Channel Estimation for Networked ISAC Systems Using Downlink Assistance and Cooperative Sensing.
abstract: This paper studies a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) networked integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, in which multiple base stations (BSs) cooperatively serve a user equipment (UE). In such systems, accurate channel state information (CSI) is critical for both communication and sensing. To achieve accurate CSI with low overhead, a two-timescale uplink channel estimation scheme is proposed. It exploits slow-varying angular parameters and fast-varying channel gains arising from large-scale and small-scale propagation, respectively. In the largetimescale phase, we exploit the temporal correlation of the channel to extract UE location via downlink cooperation and uplink cooperative sensing. During the downlink stage, the angles of the BSs are estimated at the UE using the discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) method. Based on these estimates, a codebookbased transmit beamforming is designed for uplink pilot signals. During the uplink stage, the angles and time delays of the UE are sequentially estimated at the BSs by applying the DFT method to the received directional pilot signals. Subsequently, these local estimates are forwarded to the fusion center, where an extended Kalman filter (EKF)-based fusion method is proposed to enable cooperative sensing of the UE. Based on the fused results, a codebook-based combining method is designed to enhance uplink reception. In the small-timescale phase, we propose a cooperative sensing-aided orthogonal matching pursuit (CSAOMP) algorithm, which leverages the location prior obtained from the largetimescale phase to enable channel estimation. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms benchmarks in channel estimation accuracy and achieves performance approaching that under ideal CSI conditions.

title: LLM-Empowered Covert Control in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks.
abstract: Low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs) are expected to support safety-critical control, yet they face a core challenge that reliable closed-loop performance must be guaranteed under explicit covert communication constraints and pronounced mobility. In such networks, a UAV must deliver control packets while remaining undetectable to an active warden. In this paper, we investigate a sensing-assisted covert wireless control system in which a UAV equipped with integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) capability serves multiple ground-controlled plants in the presence of a mobile warden. The design objective is to ensure linear quadratic regulator (LQR) performance while satisfying covertness requirements under transmit-power and mobility constraints. To cope with the resulting sophisticated optimization problem, we develop an end-to-end beamforming framework based on an encoding-decoding network that maps historical channel information to predictive beamformers, and we further enhance its training through a large language model (LLM)-guided strategy. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme achieves lower control cost and stronger covertness than conventional deep-learning-based beamforming benchmarks in representative low-altitude scenarios.

title: Multi-Reference Nonlinear Transform Source-Channel Coding for Wireless Image Semantic Transmission.
abstract: We propose a multi-reference nonlinear transform source-channel coding (MR-NTSCC) system to improve the rate-distortion (RD) performance by introducing multi-dimensional contexts into the entropy model of the state-of-the-art (SOTA) NTSCC system. Improvements in RD performance of the proposed MR-NTSCC system are particularly significant in high-resolution wireless image transmission under low bandwidth constraints, compared with the existing NTSCC+ system. The proposed multi-reference entropy model leverages correlations within the latent representation in both spatial and channel dimensions. In the spatial dimension, the latent representation is divided into anchors and non-anchors in a checkerboard pattern, where anchors serve as reference to estimate the mutual information between anchors and non-anchors. In the channel dimension, the latent representation is partitioned into multiple groups, and features in previous groups are analyzed to estimate the mutual information between features in previous and current groups. Taking mutual information into account, the entropy model provides an accurate estimation on the entropy, which enables efficient bandwidth allocation and enhances RD performance. Comprehensive experiments are conducted to verify the peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) performance of the proposed MR-NTSCC model superior to SOTA methods over both additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel and Rayleigh fading channel.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Spatial-Temporal Topological Decoupling Method in Battery-Free Sensor Networks.
abstract: The Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT) technology makes it possible to realize energy sustainable Battery-free SWIPT-enabled Sensor Network (BSSN). However, it is difficult to achieve the trade-off between scalability and long-term energy sustainability due to the dynamic spatialtemporal variations in data and energy flows. To this end, a Spatial-temporal Topological Decoupling Method in Batteryfree Sensor Networks (STD-BSN) is proposed. Specifically, the proposed approach combining Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Sparse Bayesian Learning (SBL) is presented, which constructs multi-dimensional influence weight matrices based on Historical Data Pearson Correlation Analysis (HD-PCA) and integrates AHP-derived weight vectors as prior knowledge into SBL to form an AHP-SBL model for accurate data-energy forecasting. Experimental results demonstrate that AHP-SBL achieves significant improvements in network lifetime and throughput compared to state-of-the-art approaches, with throughput enhancements of$\mathbf{8 0. 3 2 \%, ~} \mathbf{5 2. 3 4 \%, ~} \mathbf{4 9. 7 2 \%}$, and$\mathbf{2 9. 7 1 \%}$over LEACH, LEACHR, HHCA, and GWOA-CH respectively in large-scale network scenarios.

title: 3D Coverage Maximization via Aerial BS Navigation, Beamforming, and Spectrum Allocation: An Integrated DRL/Optimization Solution.
abstract: In this paper, we aim to enhance three-dimensional (3D) coverage in aerial communication systems, where an uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-mounted base station (UAV-BS) supports downlink transmission to aerial users (AUs). Unlike existing works that assume an idealized isotropic antenna at the UAV-BS, we consider a practical directional antenna whose gain varies with elevation angle. After deriving an analytical expression for the antenna gain, we formulate the 3D coverage maximization problem as a Markov decision process (MDP) to jointly optimize the UAV-BS navigation, beam pattern, and spectrum allocation. Then, we propose a deep reinforcement learning-based algorithm, termed integrated learning/optimization for aerial coverage maximization (ILO-ACM), which integrates spectrum allocation into the sequential decision-making process of the MDP to overcome the hybrid action space and dimension imbalance problem. Simulation results verify that the proposed ILO-ACM algorithm achieves substantial coverage performance gains compared to benchmark schemes.

title: Near-Field Beam-Split-Aware Channel Estimation in THz Massive MIMO-OTFS Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem of nearfield terahertz (THz) channel estimation in massive multipleinput multiple-output (MIMO) orthogonal time-frequency space (OTFS) systems under the impact of the beam split phenomenon. We first derive the frequency-domain input-output relationship of a massive MIMO-OTFS system in the presence of near field beam split. Subsequently, the near-field channel estimation problem is formulated as a sparse recovery problem, for which a beam-split-aware dictionary is constructed. By explicitly modeling beam-split effects within the dictionary, conventional compressed sensing algorithms can be directly leveraged for channel state information (CSI) estimation in THz regimes, without requiring customized beam-split-aware estimators. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed dictionary enables accurate and efficient sparse estimation of the near-field CSI in THz OTFS systems.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Array Configuration and Signal Processing for RIS-Assisted Integrated Sensing and Communication Systems.
abstract: In richly scattering environments such as intelligent transportation and intelligent manufacturing factory, the line-ofsight paths in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems are frequently blocked, which significantly degrades sensing accuracy. Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) has emerged as a promising technology to reshape the wireless propagation environment to improve ISAC performance. However, the full activation of RIS elements entails high power costs and heavy channel estimation burdens, which makes it difficult to preserve large aperture gains and high angular resolution. To address this challenge, we propose a coprime sparse RIS (CS-RIS) array configuration and develop a convolutional neural network (CNN)–based signal processing algorithm for the azimuth and elevation angles of multiple targets in richly scattering environments. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared with traditional equally spaced RIS array configuration, the proposed CS-RIS achieves significant gains in both unambiguous range and angular resolution. Moreover, the proposed CNN-based signal processing algorithm significantly outperforms the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm in target estimation accuracy.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Deep Learning-Powered Behavioral Authentication and Anomaly Detection for UAV Systems.
abstract: Exploiting Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) path information to monitor trajectory behavior provides a powerful means to ensure in-flight UAV authenticity, detect anomalies and identify malicious control or spoofed commands before they cause severe consequences. In this paper, we propose a novel behaviorbased UAV authentication and anomaly detection framework that leverages high-fidelity and real-world-inspired flight scenarios to obtain a comprehensive trajectory dataset. From the resulting dataset, behavioral features are extracted and processed by a deep learning classification pipeline that captures temporal dependencies and enables continuous real-time authentication under diverse mission conditions, without relying on predefined paths or static communication features. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed deep learning-based authentication approaches outperform other existing approaches in terms of precision, recall and F1-score, especially the LSTM-based authentication scheme by achieving 96% precision and 95% recall in detecting suspicious UAVs.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: CRLB and Parameter Estimation for OFDM-ISAC with Non-Uniform Sparse Resource Allocation.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) holds great promise in expanding the applications of wireless communication networks. However, in current communicationcentric systems, the time-frequency resources available for sensing may be limited, and also usually non-uniformly and sparsely distributed across the time-frequency domain. Such a non-uniformity destroys the “thumbtack-shaped” ambiguity function of the orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveform, leading to degraded sensing performance. To this end, this paper explores the parameter estimation algorithm for OFDM-ISAC systems with non-uniform sparse resource allocation. Specifically, for the single target case, we derive the closed-form Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) for parameter estimation as a function of resource indices. Furthermore, we show that simply filling unused resource locations with zeros and applying the classic periodogram estimation is equivalent to maximum likelihood (ML) estimation, which is asymptotically optimal. For the multi-target case, we generate a virtual resource using the autocorrelation function of the original signal, which exhibits a significantly larger virtual bandwidth compared to the original signal, at the cost of higher peak-to-sidelobe ratio (PSLR). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms the conventional periodogram method for non-uniform sparse resource allocation.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: A Novel Pilot Scheme for Uplink Channel Estimation in XL-MIMO Systems.
abstract: This paper designs a novel pilot scheme for extralarge massive MIMO (XL-MIMO) systems, by leveraging the spatial non-stationarity introduced by the large aperture of the extremely large aperture arrays (ELAA). The spatial nonstationarity results in distinct visibility for different users at ELAA, particularly those located far apart, which reduces inter-user interference. This property motivates our novel pilot scheme to group users with distinct visibility regions to share the same frequency subcarriers for channel estimation, hence reducing pilot overhead while accommodating numerous users. Specifically, the proposed pilot scheme employs frequencydivision multiplexing for inter-group channel estimation, while intra-group users - benefiting from strong spatial orthogonality from the distinct visibility region - are distinguished by shifted cyclic codes, similar to code-division multiplexing. Additionally, we propose a low-complexity channel estimation algorithm within a turbo Bayesian inference framework, where the channel support of each user at the ELAA features clustered sparsity in the antenna-delay domain and is modeled by a 2 -dimensional (2-D) Markov random field. Simulations show that the proposed pilot scheme and algorithm allow the XL-MIMO system to support more users, and deliver superior channel estimation performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: HSASCom: A Point Cloud Semantic Communication System with SNR-Adaptive Hierarchical Feature Transmission.
abstract: The point cloud is widely used in applications such as autonomous driving, augmented/virtual reality (AR/VR), and digital twins. However, its large data volume, irregular structure, and inherent sparsity pose significant challenges for wireless transmission. Conventional transmission methods typically suffer from limited compression efficiency, high sensitivity to channel conditions, and substantial redundancy. In this paper, we propose a point cloud semantic communication system, HSASCom, to overcome the limitations of conventional point cloud transmission. First, we introduce an end-to-end point cloud semantic communication framework that integrates hierarchical semantic-feature extraction, SNR-adaptive transmission, and semantic-guided reconstruction. By employing a joint source-channel coding architecture, HSASCom mitigates the cliff effect and reduces redundancy. Second, we propose a dual-branch attention mechanism that jointly captures local geometric details and global semantic context. An SNR-aware unequal-error-protection strategy dynamically allocates bits to prioritize critical semantic features under low-SNR conditions and to preserve fine details at high SNR. Extensive experiments on the ShapeNet dataset demonstrate that HSASCom maintains a D1-PSNR above 36 dB and a D2-PSNR above 41 dB across a 0-20 dB SNR range, and achieves up to 70.14% average bit rate saving, thereby exhibiting superior robustness and transmission efficiency.

title: Implementation of a Broadband ISAC System Based on Real-Time Channelization and DoAAided Beamforming Optimization.
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) is a key technology for next-generation wireless systems. However, achieving real-time broadband processing and practical deployment remains a significant challenge. This paper presents a hardware-software co-design prototype system using an eight-channel antenna array and a Radio Frequency System-on-Chip (RFSoC) to bridge this gap. On the hardware side, a pipelined multi-channel channelization structure implemented in programmable logic decomposes a$\mathbf{2 0 0 ~ M H z ~ b r o a d b a n d ~ s i g n a l ~ i n t o ~ e i g h t ~} \mathbf{2 5 ~ M H z}$narrowband channels, effectively overcoming the high-throughput data bottleneck. On the software side, a joint algorithm utilizes Sample Matrix Inversion (SMI) for Direction of Arrival (DoA) estimation and Second-Order Cone Programming (SOCP) for adaptive beamforming, processing the narrowband data. Experimental results demonstrate that the system achieves accurate DoA estimation and significant interference suppression, with a suppression ratio exceeding 60 dB. Compared with other optimization methods, this method significantly improves communication performance. This work provides a practical and efficient implementation framework for broadband ISAC, facilitating the transition from theory to deployment.

title: Hybrid Reinforcement Learning for Resource Allocation in VQA-Oriented UAV Semantic Offloading.
abstract: Visual question answering (VQA) plays an important role in enhancing situational awareness, while unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) provide flexible platforms to support such semantic communication tasks. This paper investigates resource allocation for VQA in UAV-assisted semantic communication networks. In the proposed framework, both UAV and user equipment (UE) adopt deep semantic communication (DeepSC)-VQA to encode semantic features, which are then offloaded to a multi-access edge computing (MEC) server for inference. To jointly optimize the energy consumption and the latency of the whole system, we develop a hybrid proximal policy optimization (HPPO) algorithm with a tailored reward function that coordinates the UAV trajectory, radio resource allocation, and semantic offloading. Simulation results show that the HPPO-based scheme consistently outperforms conventional reinforcement learning benchmarks, achieving a superior balance between the energy consumption and the latency.

title: Cross-Splitting-Based Information Geometry Approach for Xl-Mimo Uplink Detection.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel approach called cross-splitting-based information geometry approach (CS-IGA) for signal detection in extra-large-scale multi-input and multioutput (XL-MIMO) systems. In conventional information geometry approach and the Bayes-optimal approximate message passing (AMP) method, the complexity per iteration scales linearly with$M N$, where$M$is the number of BS antennas and$N$is the number of transmitted data streams. To reduce the complexity per iteration to the order of$N^{2}$, which suits the XLMIMO, we propose a matrix splitting of the natural parameters in the posterior probability density function (PDF). The number of splittings is$N$. In deriving the CS-IGA, we show that each splitting corresponds to a computation with complexity in the order of$N$. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the conventional IGA and the Bayes-optimal AMP in terms of bit error rate (BER) performance.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Harnessing Poiseuille Flow for ISI-Resilient Molecular Communication: A Spatio-Temporal Focusing Approach.
abstract: In fluidic channels such as blood vessels, the non-uniform velocity profile of Poiseuille flow introduces severe inter-symbol interference (ISI) in molecular communication. This paper proposes an innovative “spatio-temporal focusing” transmission mechanism that harnesses rather than purely counteracts the flow's properties. By leveraging the flow's velocity gradient and molecular diffusion, we optimize the transmitter's radial release position to synchronize molecules transported in different velocity layers, enabling their focused arrival at a downstream receiver. We first establish a channel model based on the advection-diffusion equation in cylindrical coordinates. We then analytically derive the channel impulse response and an expression for the system's bit error rate (BER), for which a closed-form approximation is provided. Analytical and numerical results demonstrate that, compared to the conventional on-axis release strategy, our spatio-temporal focusing mechanism significantly reduces signal pulse broadening. This leads to a dramatic suppression of ISI and lowers the BER by several orders of magnitude. This work offers an efficient physical-layer solution to enhance the reliability of molecular communication in fluidic environments, with significant potential for applications such as targeted drug delivery and in vivo nanosensor networks.

title: Drift-Aware Updating: An Edge-Device Cooperative RL Framework for Robust and Low-Overhead BCI Adaptation.
abstract: The reliable deployment of mobile Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI) is fundamentally constrained by the perceptual nature of Electroencephalography (EEG) acquisition, where the sensed neural signals evolve continuously due to physiological, cognitive, and environmental factors, as well as the limited resources of wearable devices. While server-assisted adaptation can mitigate such perception-driven concept drift, it imposes significant communication and computational overhead. Existing solutions typically rely on rigid, periodic update schedules that fail to dynamically balance decoding accuracy against system costs. To address this, we propose a Drift-Aware Device-Server Framework driven by Reinforcement Learning (RL). In this architecture, an RL agent monitors distributional shifts in the perceptually acquired EEG signals and autonomously selects from a tiered set of maintenance actions, ranging from no-update to varying degrees of model retraining. By decoupling continuous sensing from expensive computation, the learned policy optimizes the longterm trade-off between inference reliability and resource consumption. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework outperforms static baselines, reducing computational load by$\mathbf{7 4 \%}$and data transmission by 20 % while achieving superior decoding accuracy. This establishes a scalable, energy-efficient paradigm for sustaining robust BCI operation in resource-constrained wireless networks.

title: OMP-Assisted CBAM Network-Based Channel Estimation for OTFS Systems.
abstract: Orthogonal time-frequency space (OTFS) modulation effectively supports high-mobility communication scenarios, and the sparse nature of its delay-Doppler (DD) channel makes the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm widely applicable for channel estimation. However, the performance degradation of OMP under noisy conditions motivates deep learning (DL) alternatives, which still lack effective attention mechanisms for discriminative feature extraction. This paper proposes an OMP-assisted convolutional block attention module network (O-CBAM-Net) for channel representation learning. The proposed O-CBAM-Net leverages lightweight OMP-based sparse priors and a CBAM-based dual-attention mechanism to capture the sparse locations, complex gains, and two-dimensional structural distribution of dominant propagation paths. Residual connections are incorporated to enhance feature representation and learning stability. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed O-CBAM-Net consistently outperforms OMP and DL baselines over a range of signal to noise ratios (SNRs) while maintaining a balanced performance-complexity tradeoff. Specifically, at an SNR of 20 dB, O-CBAM-Net achieves approximately a 3.5 dB normalized mean square error (NMSE) gain over OMP. In addition, strong robustness under varying mobility conditions is demonstrated.

title: Enhancing Physical Layer Security in STAR-RIS Communication Systems Assisted by UAV.
abstract: This paper investigates the physical layer security of a wireless communication system aided by an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-mounted simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS). A multiantenna access point (AP) transmits confidential messages to users in the transmission and reflection regions, respectively, in the presence of eavesdroppers. We formulate an optimization problem to maximize the system sum rate by jointly optimizing the AP's beamforming vectors and the STAR-RIS coefficients matrix. The original non-convex problem is decomposed into two tractable subproblems via an alternating optimization (AO) framework. The non-convexity issues are addressed using successive convex approximation (SCA) and semidefinite relaxation (SDR) techniques, leading to an efficient iterative algorithm that converges to a stationary point of the original problem. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms benchmark schemes in terms of sum rate while guaranteeing security. Furthermore, the flexible deployment of the STAR-RIS by the UAV provides additional performance gains.

title: Large-Language-Model Based Beamforming Prediction for Sensing-Aided Communication.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is expected to enable the fifth-generation (5G) networks to provide ubiquitous communication and sensing. However, some highdynamic scenarios hinder applications of conventional ISAC schemes owing to the high overhead. In this paper, we design a novel ISAC architecture and propose a large language model (LLM) based two-stage beamforming prediction scheme. Specifically, in the first stage, we develop an LLM-based approach to predict the future channel state information (CSI) according to the history echoes. In the second stage, according to the predicted/estimated CSI, we formulate a beamforming optimization problem to maximize the achievable sum rate. Then, we propose a Primary-dual network to handle it. Simulation results verify that, compared with the benchmarks, our proposed beamforming prediction scheme not only enjoys a higher channel prediction accuracy but also achieves a better balance between the performance and computational complexity.

title: Robust Aerial RIS-Aided Secure Transmission in LEO Satellite Systems with Beamforming and Cooperative Jamming.
abstract: This paper investigates the robust aerial reconfigurable intelligent surface (ARIS)-aided secure transmission in a low earth orbit (LEO) satellite system, where the ARIS simultaneously reflects confidential signals and emits cooperative jamming to enhance secrecy performance under imperfect channel state information. We first determine the LEO satellite trajectory and conduct theoretical modeling for the system secrecy rate (SR) under random satellite beamforming, ARIS phase shifts and cooperative jamming settings. By leveraging theories such as mean-square error, Rayleigh quotient, and second-order cone programming, we then propose a hierarchical optimization framework to obtain the optimal settings for SR maximization. Finally, extensive simulation results are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in enhancing the SR performance of the considered system.

title: Hybrid Beamforming Design for Finite-Blocklength Covert mmWave ISAC Systems.
abstract: This paper investigates the design of hybrid beamforming (HBF) for covert millimeter-wave (mmWave) integrated sensing and communication systems under finite blocklength (FBL) constraint. Specifically, a dual-function mmWave transmitter (Alice) aims to sense potential targets and communicate with multiple legitimate users (Bobs) in the presence of a malicious warden (Willie). To this end, we formulate the HBF design problem to maximize the covert sum rate (CSR) with FBL constraint, while ensuring covertness of transmission, maintaining sensing beampattern gain, and satisfying Bobs' minimum covert rate requirements. Then, we reformulate the original challenging problem into more tractable form via the penalty dual decomposition method. Subsequently, we propose a computationally efficient alternating iteration algorithm, incorporating the Riemannian exact penalty optimization, elementwise iteration, and closed-form variable updates. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed HBF design in terms of achievable CSR and computational efficiency compared to benchmark schemes.

title: Joint Localization and Orientation Assisted by Massive MIMO-OFDM Triple-Beam Fingerprints.
abstract: Wireless communication systems offer strong potential for accurate localization, and deep-learning-based fingerprinting has shown good adaptability in complex propagation environments. However, existing fingerprints are limited to static location features, and current neural network designs do not fully utilize their structural properties. To improve this, we introduce a dynamic triple-beam fingerprint (TBF) for massive multipleinput multiple-output (MIMO) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems and develop a localization and orientation awareness network (LOA-Net) designed to align with its sparse structural characteristics for joint localization and orientation estimation. We analyze the advantages of TBF for localization and orientation awareness through channel modeling. Localization is formulated as a regression task and enhanced with a masking mechanism, while orientation estimation is modeled as a multi-class classification problem using the estimated coordinates as prior information. Simulations in standard 3GPP scenarios demonstrate the high localization accuracy and the potential for effective orientation awareness.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: MFM-Enabled ISAC for 6G Networks: General Framework and Predictive Beamforming via BQNet.
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) is essential for the Low-Altitude Economy (LAE) to support seamless UAV operations. However, conventional ISAC systems struggle with multimodal data processing and semantic understanding in dynamic low-altitude environments. This paper proposes a multimodal fusion model (MFM)-ISAC framework, where a large model is deeply embedded into the closed-loop sensing-communication interaction rather than acting as a backend tool. The framework projects multimodal inputs into a shared latent space and aligns asynchronous streams for realtime decision-making. Building on the resulting unified and temporally aligned representation, we developed the ISAC-beamaware query network (BQNet) for predictive beamforming, which maps sensing sequences directly to optimal beams using temporal harmonization and codebook-informed queries, bypassing explicit channel estimation and beam sweeping. Experiments on a custom low-altitude UAV mmWave dataset showed that ISAC-BQNet achieves$\mathbf{7 9. 9 5 {\%}}$Top-1 and 96.35% Top-3 accuracy, outperforming representative baseline models.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Stackelberg-Contract-Based Dependent Task Offloading and Resource Pricing in PVEC Networks.
abstract: Parked Vehicle-assisted Edge Computing (PVEC) utilizes idle parked vehicles (PVs) to offer edge computing services for user vehicles (UVs), effectively reducing latency and energy consumption. Nevertheless, uneven resource distribution and inter-task dependencies in PVEC networks may cause inefficient task offloading and unfair resource pricing. To overcome these challenges, this paper presents a Stackelberg game and Contract theory-based Dependent task Offloading and resource Pricing (SCDOP) framework. In this framework, UVs partially offload their dependent tasks to Roadside Units (RSUs) managed by an SDN controller, while overloaded RSUs will transmit the tasks to nearby PVs. The interactions among RSUs, UVs, and PVs are modeled by Stackelberg game and contract theory, and the economic properties of SCDOP are mathematically proven. A social welfare maximization problem is formulated and a Particle Swarm Optimization Plus Genetic (PSOPG) algorithm is developed to derive near-optimal solutions. Simulation results show that PSOPG achieves higher task completion rates and greater social welfare than benchmark schemes.

title: Energy Efficiency Maximization in Hybrid Bit-Semantic Communication Networks.
abstract: Semantic communications (SCs) have revealed significant potential in improving transmission efficiency by conveying semantic information rather than raw bit signals. However, the additional computational overhead introduced at transceivers makes it challenging to achieve high energy efficiency in deep learning (DL)-enabled SC systems. In this paper, we first define a semantic energy efficiency (S-EE) metric by jointly considering the semantic rate, transmission power, computing power, signal processing power, and circuit power at both the transmitter and receiver sides. In contrast, existing studies typically consider only one side of power consumption and thus overlook the effects of the semantic extraction ratio and computational consumption on S-EE. We then formulate an S-EE maximization problem by jointly optimizing the semantic extraction ratio, transmission rate, and bandwidth allocation. An alternating optimizationbased scheme is proposed to solve this non-convex problem. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed SC-based scheme achieves significant improvement in terms of S-EE compared to the conventional communication.

title: Near-Field XL-MiMO for ISAC: Joint Multi-User Channel Sensing and Predictive Beamforming.
abstract: Near-field (NF) extremely large-scale multiple-input-multiple-output (XL-MIMO) enables new opportunities for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). In this paper, we first propose a generic OFDM-ISAC scheme to sense and communicate with multiple mobile users simultaneously, which includes discovery phase and tracking phase. In the discovery phase, noting that the radar received signal at each antenna suffers from different Doppler shift in the NF scenario, the radar parameter estimation is more challenging than its counterpart in the far-field (FF). To address this problem, we divide the XL antenna array into multiple subarrays by which the channel between each subarray and user can be modeled approximately as the FF condition. Then, the classical FF sensing methods are utilized to estimate the radar parameters of all subarrays. Moreover, the iterative parallel interference cancellation is employed to eliminate the interference among subarrays, and the information fusion is efficiently performed to recover the speed and motion direction. In the tracking phase, based on the estimated velocity, predictive beamforming is designed for mobile users to assist the communication. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed structure is verified by numerical simulations.

title: Channel Estimation and MA Trajectory Design with Time Constraint.
abstract: Movable antenna (MA) has emerged as a promising technology to enhance communication performance. However, since the movement speed of MA is practically constrained by mechanical drivers and the channel coherence time is limited, the time overhead for antenna movement in channel estimation and performance improvement can significantly affect the effective rate of MA systems in practice. To address this issue, we propose in this paper to jointly design the MA's trajectories, including the trajectory for obtaining channel measurements and that for moving to the rate-optimal position, to maximize the average effective rate of an MA-aided receiver subject to the given transmission block duration by a two time-scale optimization approach. Specifically, the number of channel measurements as well as the MA's trajectory for obtaining them are first optimized in the long term based on the known channel distribution, while the number of moving steps as well as the MA's trajectory for moving to the rate-optimal position are adaptively designed in the short term to cater to the instantaneous channel realizations, thus simplifying the design complexity and yet providing high adaptability to channel variations. A key challenge in our short-term design is accurately reconstructing the channel map from measurements at only a subset of antenna positions. By exploiting the spatial channel correlations over positions in the moving region, we propose a kernel-based regression (KBR) method to reconstruct the channel map. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme outperforms the fixed-position antenna (FPA) system and other benchmark MA designs that neglect the antenna movement time under various channel setups.
conference_title: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference

title: Joint Trajectory-Resource Scheduling for UAV-USV Collaborative Perception in Dynamic Maritime Environments.
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) are increasingly deployed for wide-area and persistent maritime target perception in applications such as search and rescue, environmental surveillance, and navigation safety. However, such systems face significant challenges due to dynamic ocean conditions, unstable communication links, and stringent on-board energy constraints, which limit their operational endurance and perception integrity. To address these issues, this paper focuses on the cooperative perception of partially submerged maritime targets using a UAV-USV team and tackles the joint problem of trajectory planning and communication resource allocation under realistic ocean current disturbances. We develop a system model that incorporates target and platform mobility influenced by currents and formulate an energy-efficient optimization framework that ensures a minimum perception quality. A Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG)-based solution is designed to enable decentralized coordination and adaptive decision-making. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach reduces total system energy consumption by 15% - 20% compared to a baseline method while maintaining reliable target perception performance in dynamic maritime settings.

title: UAV-Relay and UAV-SAR Assisted ISAC System for Target Areas Imaging.
abstract: This paper investigates a novel integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system assisted by a UAV-relay and a UAV-SAR for target areas imaging. The system comprises a UAVSAR equipped with an ISAC system for high-resolution imaging of target areas, and a UAV-relay that forwards the collected data to the data center when the direct link is obstructed or insufficient for high-rate SAR data transmission. To minimize the total system energy consumption while ensuring system performance, we formulate a joint optimization problem over the UAV-SAR's trajectory, flight velocity, beamforming design, and the UAV-relay's deployment, explicitly incorporating constraints on SAR image SNR for reliable imaging and communication data rate for timely sensing information transmission. To address the non-convexity of the formulated problem, a penalty-based block coordinate descent (BCD) algorithm is developed, which iteratively solves a sequence of convex subproblems. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly reduces energy consumption by 19.74 % compared with the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm.

title: Semantic-Aware Video Communication: Enhancing Traditional and Deep Video Encoders.
abstract: Video semantic communication (VSC) offers a novel approach to compress videos at aggressive rates. However, existing VSC methods primarily emphasize intra-frame semantic importance while ignoring the inter-frame semantic importance. To address this issue, we propose a semantic-aware video communication (SAVC) scheme, where encoding parameters such as compression rate and key frame interval are adaptively adjusted for each group of pictures (GOP) in the video based on interframe semantic importance. In the proposed scheme, GOPs are adaptively encoded with semantic-aware encoding parameters, followed by reconstruction at the receiver. First, we use a deep neural network to extract semantic features and introduce a semantic importance metric based on semantic similarity between GOPs, where higher similarity indicates lower importance. Then, we formulate an video encoding parameter optimization problem that balances video quality and bitrate, and we design a proximal policy optimization algorithm for parameter selection (PPOPS) to solve the optimization problem. Simulation results show that the proposed SAVC scheme can reduce at most 8.188% and 8.021% Bjøntegaard Delta rate in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity index measure over baseline methods.

title: Antenna Coding Optimization for Pixel Antenna Empowered Wireless Communication Using Deep Learning with Heterogeneous Multi-Head Selection.
abstract: Pixel antenna is a promising antenna technology that enables flexible adjustment of radiation characteristics and enhancement of wireless systems through antenna coding. This work proposes a novel deep learning-based antenna coding optimization algorithm. Specifically, the proposed algorithm is supported by a heterogeneous multi-head selection mechanism, whose main idea is to train multiple neural networks based on various coding schemes and select the one that leads to the best system performance. Unlike traditional heuristic searchingbased algorithms that require high computational complexity to achieve satisfactory performance, the proposed data-driven deep learning approach can achieve 98 % of the performance achieved by the searching-based algorithms with significantly reduced computational complexity. Results demonstrate that in pixel antenna empowered single-input single-output systems, the proposed algorithm achieves a computational speed 81 times faster than the searching-based algorithm. For more complex pixel antenna empowered multiple-input multiple-output systems, the computational speed is 297 times faster than the existing searching-based algorithm. Benefiting from the high performance and low computational complexity, this algorithm demonstrates the significant potential of pixel antennas as a novel and practical technology to enhance wireless systems.
